into `packReadings`, an array that lives and dies inside the episode loop.

So the sentence "the store serves one record per request" has been quoted for four rounds without anyone
being able to say **which** record, and two very different stores produce it: one where a single record
carries every request and fourteen are never rendered, and one where the fifteen rotate. The first is a
store with one rule in it; the second is a store of fifteen. The mean is identical.

**Why it mattered at R93 and not before.** Every earlier arm changed the store and read the score.
R93 changes the *serving*, and a serving experiment whose outcome depends on *which* records reached
which tasks cannot be explained by an aggregate. Concretely, the three questions the readback will ask —
was the record served to a failed task ever the one about that task; did the record that carried the
most requests also carry the most passes; how many of the fifteen ever reached a prompt — have no
answer in any artefact this lane has ever written.

**The fix.** `UseObservation` gains an optional `ids`, the driver records `pack.ids` at both push sites,
and `servedCensus` reduces the run to `requests`, `identified`, `distinct`, `meanPerRequest`,
`maxPerRequest` and a per-id count sorted by id. A request that recorded no ids stays `unidentified`
rather than being read as an empty pack, because a run that did not instrument is not a run that served
nothing. The planted-arm site records the store's ids only: a planted rule is not a store item and an
invented id would join to nothing in `storeItems`.

**The rule this adds.**

> When a treatment is a *selection*, the artefact has to record the selection and not its size. A mean
> over what was served cannot distinguish a store that is used from a store that is not.

## 34.122 `supportTasks` is one by construction, and the competitor's winning cell needs three

**The defect.** ALTK-Evolve's strongest configuration keeps only rules taught by **≥3 distinct training
tasks** (`sup3`), and it is the configuration that flips sign between retail and airline. This store
computes `supportTasks` (`countDistinctTasks(item.evidence)`), carries it into the artefact, and
admission reads a `support` scalar. R92's fifteen items read:

| field | value | what it can be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `supportTasks` | **1**, fifteen times | the dedupe key is the **normalized statement** (`dedupeKeyOf`), and one correction produces one statement |
| `evidence` | 1, fifteen times | one task, one correction, one item |
| `trust` | 0.9, fifteen times | a constant, so `confidence` is **0.6165** for all fifteen |
| `kind` | `exemplar`, fifteen times | the raw unit |

Two failures of the same *shape* — the same tool sequence with different order ids — produce two
statements that differ in every token that matters to the dedupe key and are therefore two items with
support 1 each. The recurrence axis exists in the record, is computed at write time, is carried into
every artefact, and **cannot be populated** by any correction this lane produces. R55.1's
`packMode: prefix` with `minEvidence: 3` was blocked on exactly this ("no item in any store has support
3"), and Appendix M's "0 of 7 admitted by recurrence" is the same fact counted from the other end.

**Why the constant confidence follows.** `trust` and `support` are both 0.9 for every item because both
are functions of (one observation, one trusted source). An admission rule that assigns the same number
to every item cannot select among them, which is why every item in R92's store is `confidence-cleared`
and none is ranked.

**What the literature does instead, and it is not a threshold.** Agent Workflow Memory induces a
workflow from **several** trajectories and abstracts the task-specific values out of it; ExpeL merges
repeated insights with `UPVOTE`/`DOWNVOTE` operators over a pool; ALTK keeps the rules three tasks
agreed on. All three *aggregate before storing*. This lane stores first and never aggregates, so the
number its admission reads is a constant by construction rather than by measurement.

**What this does not license.** Lowering `minEvidence` to 1, which would admit everything and turn the
knob into decoration. The repair is a merge step over the corrections — two corrections whose action
sequences agree are one rule with support 2 — and it is registered as an arm rather than applied as a
default, because it changes what a published number measured.

## 34.123 The pair differed in an agent class, and the wrapper has never been run against an empty pack

**What the artefacts say.** R93 ran both legs of one dispatch and its two eval phases name different
agents:

```
memory leg     "agent": "microglia_agent", "memory_url": "http://127.0.0.1:33249"
reference leg  "agent": "llm_agent",       "memory_url": ""
```

`tau2-driver.ts` chooses between them on `MEMORY`: with the store, the agent is `microglia_agent` and it
is pointed at the recall facade; without it, the agent is τ²'s own `llm_agent` and no facade is started.
So the paired delta of **−2.50pp** is a delta between *(wrapper + pack)* and *(stock agent)*, not between
*(pack)* and *(no pack)*.

**Why this is a defect and not a detail.** `microglia_agent` is documented as additive — it subclasses
`LLMAgent`, wraps `generate_next_message`, and prepends one system message on a copy of the state
(`microglia_agent.py`, "The memory is not a tool and not a policy change"). If that documentation is
complete, the wrapper is inert and the delta belongs to the pack. **Nothing in this record demonstrates
that it is complete**, because no arm has ever run `microglia_agent` against a facade that returns an
empty pack. Two consequences follow:

- the finding "the memory costs 2.5 points" is really "the memory *or the wrapper* costs 2.5 points";
- the 2.17× bill is attributed to the pack, when part of it could belong to the wrapper's call pattern
  (the memory leg made 2,667 calls against the control's 2,726, so the wrapper is not making *more* calls
  — but the three-way split of the bill has never been measured).

**The arm this needs, and it is cheap.** A third leg: `microglia_agent` pointed at a facade that answers
every request with an empty pack. Same class, same message shape, no content. Three cells then decompose
what two could not:

| cell | agent | pack | what it isolates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reference (R93) | `llm_agent` | none | the stock baseline |
| **scaffold (new)** | `microglia_agent` | **empty** | **the wrapper, alone** |
| memory (R93) | `microglia_agent` | 15 records | the pack, given the wrapper |

One leg, 160 episodes, **~$0.38** — the cheapest arm in this project's history, and it decides whether the
next four rounds are about retrieval or about the agent.

**Why it was not run in R93.** The reference leg is defined as "the same driver with `TAU_MEMORY=false`",
and that flag selects the stock agent because a facade with nothing to serve is a component that can
fail. That is a defensible engineering choice and an indefensible experimental one, and the difference
only became visible when the pair came back resolvable enough to ask *which* of the two legs moved.

**The rule this adds.**

> When a treatment is delivered through a component, the control has to run that component empty. A pair
> that differs in the delivery mechanism and in the content attributes both to the content, and the
> attribution cannot be recovered from the artefact afterwards.

## 34.124 The control's emptiness is declared rather than observed, and the arm costs 2.17× what §34.123 said

**What was built.** `TAU_SCAFFOLD=empty-pack` resolves to a third arm kind — `memory` / `reference` /
`scaffold` — through one function (`tau2-arm-kind.ts`) that both the driver and the artefact writer read,
so the process that runs the episodes and the file that describes them cannot disagree about which arm
was bought. Contradictory settings are refused rather than ranked: `TAU_MEMORY=false` beside
`TAU_SCAFFOLD=empty-pack` names the stock agent *and* the wrapper, the losing variable leaves no trace in
the artefact, and a silent precedence would produce a record nobody can audit afterwards.

The scaffold leg skips the learn half entirely rather than pinning it. A pin replays a store; this arm has
no store to replay, and paying for 74 learn episodes to produce records nobody reads would cost the arm
its own reason for existing — it is the decomposition leg, and the decomposition is one held-out half wide.

**The problem the implementation exposed, which the registration had not.** Two blocking gates exist to
catch exactly the state this arm is defined by. `V0-instrument-ready` refuses a pipeline whose every stage
carried nothing, because on a memory arm an empty pipeline is a broken chain. `V1-pack-not-empty` refuses
a mean of zero rules per question, because on a memory arm that is either a store with nothing servable or
a facade dropping what it was offered. A scaffold arm is a broken memory arm to both.

Three dispositions were available and only one is admissible:

| disposition | what it makes the arm | why not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| waive both gates for the arm | unmeasurable | a gate that stands down for one arm is the vacuous pass this record keeps finding: `V6` and `V7` fire on an empty control list and certify nothing, and all seventeen published BIRD artefacts carry `V6` that way |
| omit the gates from the arm | silent | omitting a gate is a statement, and here the statement would be "this run's pipeline is not graded", which is exactly the run whose pipeline matters most |
| **invert both gates** | **falsifiable** | **chosen** |

`declaredEmptyVerdict` requires all five stages to be zero and refuses the arm the moment one carries
anything: "the arm declared an empty store and its servable stage carried 3: this is no longer the control
it was registered as". `V1` requires the mean pack to be exactly zero, so a scaffold arm that injects one
rule fails the gate that would have passed a memory arm. The exemption is inverted rather than granted,
which is the only form that keeps the declaration from being unfalsifiable.

**Why a declaration and not an inference.** `funnel.stored === 0` is true of a scaffold arm and of a
memory arm whose distillation died, and the two need opposite readings — one is the arm doing what it was
registered for, the other is a run with no result. The flag travels as `declaredEmptyStore`, present only
on the arm that made it and absent everywhere before it: absence reads as "not declared" rather than as
`false`, because a boolean written into every record would be a measurement about arms that were never
asked.

**The cost estimate in §34.123 was wrong by 3.2×, and the error is the reasoning the arm exists to
correct.** §34.123 said "one leg, 160 episodes, ~$0.38" — the reference leg's price. The scaffold leg
cannot cost that, because it runs the wrapper: R93 billed the memory leg at **$0.8276** against the
reference leg's **$0.3807**, a **2.17×** ratio driven by 36.2% more prompt tokens and a cache hit rate
14.8pp lower. The ratio *is* the quantity this arm prices, so an estimate that assumed it away would have
been an estimate of the wrapper being free. The registration states **~$1.21** for the pair and records
the superseded number beside it.

**What the arm still cannot certify, restated because it is the reason to run it anyway.** At n = 40
paired tasks the lane resolves **19.8pp** at d = 0.20 and **17.1pp** at d = 0.30. R101 therefore separates
"the wrapper costs about twenty points" from "the wrapper costs less than this sample can see"; it cannot
certify a 2.5pp wrapper cost, and no trial count changes that, because `pass^4` is one binary per task. The
distinction is still the one that decides whether the next four rounds are about retrieval or about the
agent, and it is the cheapest question in the queue.

## 34.125 Supply was not the constraint, and the instrument that says so was built the day before

**The hypothesis R99 was registered to test.** R92's store held fifteen records, R91's readback showed
R89 and R90 producing twelve and fifteen from the same fifty-seven tasks, and every round since R85 had
read the memory's nulls as a supply problem: too few rules, too narrow a pack, too little of the question
covered. R99 changed one variable — `distillScope: edited` to `all`, which turns the fifteen corrections a
pinned learn half produces into the seventy-three that every task produces — and stated its criterion
before the dispatch: **`< 0.700` closes the supply line**.

The arm returned **0.625** against R93's **0.700** and the control's **0.725**. The line closes.

**Why this is a stronger result than its three-task size, and where the strength comes from.** A three-task
move at n = 40 is barely above this lane's own noise floor (R92 0.650 against R93 0.700 at essentially one
store). What makes it a refutation rather than a draw is that **every instrument built to explain the
old failure moved in the direction the theory predicted, and the score moved the other way**:

| reading | R93 (15 records) | R99 (73 records) | direction the theory wanted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| requests served | 161 of 162 | 161 of 161 | unchanged, both perfect |
| mean items per pack | 1.081 | 1.292 | up |
| coverage p10 / p50 / p90 | 0.129 / 0.227 / 0.368 | 0.176 / 0.333 / 0.529 | **up, at every quantile** |
| zero-coverage pairs | 0 of 174 | 0 of 208 | unchanged, never the failure |
| `pass^4` | **0.700** | **0.625** | down |

The "the record only mentions a fifth of the question" reading was the sharpest thing this project had
said about its own defect, and R99 tuned exactly that number by a third and lost three tasks. A theory that
is tested in its own currency and comes back inverted is not a null result; it is the theory being wrong.

**What the widening actually was, and why the word "supply" is a half-truth.** The `provenance` block
separates the store by the trajectory each record came from: R93 held **15 items edited, 0 passed**; R99 held
**15 edited, 58 passed**. `distillScope: all` does not find more failures in the same learn half — the
failures are fixed by the pin — it asks the seventy-four tasks that ran for a rule either way, and the
fifty-nine that passed answer too. So R99 is *the same fifteen repair records plus fifty-eight rules
described from successful attempts*, and its −7.5pp is a statement about success-derived guidance.

This is the difference between a measurement and a label. "Five times the store" invites the repair "make
it smaller"; "seventy-nine per cent of the store is now descriptions of what one successful attempt did,
carrying that attempt's own arguments" invites the repair "that is not a rule". The second is supported by
this project's own history — R90 built a guard because a claim was eating the references the agent needed,
and a record written from a pass carries `order_abc123` where the next task needs `order_def456` — and it is
the reading the next two arms are built on: R98 removes relevance (unrelated records at matched length) and
merge-by-shape removes the per-instance text (53 routines instead of 73 instances).

**What the two new censuses added, which the mean could not.** Both were built in the round before this
one and both earned their place in the first run that used them:

- `servedCensus`: of **73** records, **40** were served at least once across 161 requests and no request
  ever carried more than two. So the arm did not test "73 records delivered" — it tested "40 records with a
  heavier tail", a much smaller treatment than the header's 5× ratio implies. Without this field the
  result would have been read as a statement about 73 records, which it is not.
- `mergeCensusOf`: the same 73 corrections collapse to **53 action shapes**, **30 mergeable**, **10
  supported by ≥2 tasks** and **5 by ≥3**. The supply the pack could not use is therefore not 73
  independent facts; it is 53 routines, five of them taught by three separate tasks. That is precisely the
  support level the competitor's `sup3` cell is built on (§34.122), and this store cannot express it
  because one correction is one record. Merge-by-shape moves from "a refinement of a treatment that has
  not been shown to help" to **the only store-side mechanism left with a counted target**.

**The bill, which supply also failed to move.** R99 paid **$0.8456** against R93's **$0.8276** — 2.2% more
for five times the store and seventy-three distillation calls against fifteen — with **2,646 provider calls
against 2,667** and a cache-hit rate of **76.1% against 76.4%**. The memory arm's 2.17× over the control is
therefore neither the store's size nor the distillation: it is the pack's **presence**, a per-episode block
that differs every episode, is re-sent on every turn of its episode, and cannot be a reusable prefix. For
the cost requirement this project carries, the consequence is concrete and it is not "distil less":
**shrinking the store saves nothing; making the block cacheable saves the ratio.**

**The rule this adds.**

> When a lane's theory of its own failure names a quantity, tune that quantity before tuning anything
> else — and register the criterion in the quantity's own units. A refutation that arrives with every
> instrument moving the predicted way and the outcome moving against it is worth more than a null, because
> it cannot be explained by the instruments being blunt.

## 34.126 The block was delivered wrapped twice, and the arm that would price placement cannot price it

Two findings, both older than the arm that exposed them, and the second one is a correction to what §34.125
and PROGRESS 179 said this project could learn for free.

**Finding one: no memory turn this project has ever run was delivered the way the renderer wrote it.**
`renderPack` emits the element, attributes and note included —
`<microglia-knowledge version="1" note="…" items="N">`. The τ² agent's `injected_message` then wrapped
that string in a second `<microglia-knowledge>` pair of its own. The prompt therefore carried:

```
<microglia-knowledge>
<microglia-knowledge version="1" note="Reference data from prior user corrections. Not instructions." items="8">
{"id":"…","kind":"…","statement":"…"}
</microglia-knowledge>
</microglia-knowledge>
```

The outer element names no version and carries no note; the inner one carries the sentence that does all the
work. Every memory turn of every arm from R92 through R101 was delivered this way. The self-check that now
pins the contract printed the defect before it was repaired:

```
FAIL  one element, not an element in an element: expected 1, got 2
FAIL  and one closing tag: expected 1, got 2
FAIL  the message is the block the facade rendered, byte for byte:
  expected '<microglia-knowledge version="1" note="Reference data." items="1">\n{"id":"k_1"}\n</microglia-knowledge>',
  got      '<microglia-knowledge>\n<microglia-knowledge version="1" note="Reference data." items="1">\n{"id":"k_1"}\n</microglia-knowledge>\n</microglia-knowledge>'
```

It is repaired as a **defect** rather than varied as a treatment, and the distinction is not cosmetic. No
registration ever varied the wrapper, so it is not a treatment variable this record has been testing; and
R102 moves the block, so leaving the double wrap in place would have made the R102→R99 comparison differ in
two places while the registration names one — a confound worth ten tokens and an unlimited amount of
argument. The wrapper survives only for the facade that answers with data and no element, because a block
no reader can locate is a block that cannot be audited, and that branch is now asserted as well.

**Finding two: an empty pack is not a cheap pack, and R101 therefore prices nothing.** PROGRESS 179 ended
with a free discriminating test: if the scaffold leg (wrapper, empty pack) billed near the control's $0.38
the premium was the block's presence, and if it billed near the memory arm's $0.83 it was the wrapper's call
pattern. That test is void, and the reason is in the agent rather than in the arithmetic:

```python
pack = self.pack_for(state, text if isinstance(text, str) else "")
if pack:                      # an empty pack injects nothing at all
    state.system_messages = list(state.system_messages) + [injected_message(pack)]
```

An arm whose pack is empty sends the **reference arm's prompt byte for byte**. Its bill will land near $0.38
whatever the truth is, and reading that as "the block's presence is the cause" would be reading the
wrapper's own definition back as evidence. R101 remains exactly what it was registered as — a behavioural
control that separates the wrapper from the pack — and it prices nothing.

**What the discriminating instrument is instead.** The question is mechanical: does the provider cache the
second system message or does the prefix end before it? A mechanical fact is cheaper to measure than to
guess, and `cache-placement.ts` measures it directly — four prompt shapes over nine growing turns, reading
`prompt_cache_hit_tokens` per call. Thirty-six calls of a few thousand prompt tokens is **cents** against
the **$0.83** an arm costs to ask the same thing and then be unable to attribute the answer, because a
treatment that moves the block also changes the prompt.

The four shapes and the four states are deliberately not two. `system-second` is what the lane sends;
`system-merged` puts the block inside the single system message, which is the minimal repair if the message
boundary is the thing; `first-turn` rides the task statement instead of the policy, which is where ExpeL puts
its insights rather than where AWM puts its workflows (§Appendix X), and is the only shape that changes the
block's *illocutionary* position. The verdict can also come back `placement-is-free` — the block was cached
all along and the arm's premium is something else — or `block-never-cached` — no placement fixes it. Two of
the four outcomes refuse R102 rather than confirm it, which is the property that makes the probe worth
running.

**The rule this adds.**

> A control that removes a treatment by making it empty prices nothing when the treatment's cost is carried
> by the text. Ask what the control actually sends before reading its bill as a decomposition: an arm that
> injects nothing is a second copy of the control, and the only thing it can measure is behaviour.

## 34.127 The block is cached where it sits: R102 is refused by the probe it was registered on, and the probe was wrong twice first

R102 was registered as a cost treatment — move the block, and the 2.17× goes away — on the strength of
PROGRESS 179's decomposition: 99.9% of the premium is uncached prompt tokens, ~1.1k extra on each call. Before
spending $0.83 on a treatment whose mechanism was a guess, `cache-placement.ts` priced the mechanism: four
prompt shapes, nine growing turns, the provider's own `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` per call. Three dispatches
were needed, and the first two are the interesting part.

**Run 1 (`43489549678`) — `placement-is-free`, and not for a good reason.** All four shapes shared one
synthetic policy, so the control's calls warmed a prefix the next shape's *first* call then read:

```
control        prompt/call   5027  uncached/call first  4051  steady 606.5
system-second  prompt/call   6524  uncached/call first  1964  steady 617.5
```

A 6,524-token prompt billed 1,964 uncached while a 5,027-token prompt billed 4,051 is not a fact about either
shape: it is the control's cache being spent by the second shape. The steady state was unaffected — each shape's
prefix is internally consistent — so the verdict was right by accident.

**Run 2 (`43491046858`) — `block-never-cached`, and also not for a good reason.** Each shape now had its own
policy, which removed the sharing and exposed the other uncontrolled variable: five seconds between calls is
not long enough for a written cache entry to be readable. Only the control had a prefix written by the previous
run, and it alone read low:

```
control        prompt/call   5027  uncached/call first   211  steady 180.5
system-second  prompt/call   6524  uncached/call first  5548  steady 617.5
system-merged  prompt/call   6524  uncached/call first  5548  steady 617.5
first-turn     prompt/call   6524  uncached/call first  5548  steady 617.5
```

Delta 437 a call, over the tolerance, verdict `block-never-cached` — a conclusion about the provider's
bookkeeping, drawn from the one shape whose policy happened to be warm from an earlier dispatch.

**Run 3 (`43492274964`) — `placement-is-free`, on an instrument that has been made to fail.** A warmup call at
the longest history warms every shorter prefix at once, because a cache is a prefix; the wait is fifteen
seconds, which is what run 2's own numbers say an entry needs.

| shape | prompt/call | first uncached | steady uncached | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control` | 5,027 | 211 | **180.5** | — |
| `system-second` | 6,524 | 172 | **211.5** | +31 |
| `system-merged` | 6,524 | 172 | **211.5** | +31 |
| `first-turn` | 6,524 | 172 | **211.5** | +31 |

**The block adds 1,497 prompt tokens per call and 31 uncached ones — 2% of itself.** It is cached in all three
placements, the second system message is not a boundary the provider refuses to carry, and moving it buys
nothing. R102.1 is not dispatched: `placement-is-free` is one of the two states the probe was built to refuse
it with, and the refusal cost **$0.09** across three dispatches instead of **$0.83** for an arm whose delta
nobody could have attributed.

**What this costs the record.** §34.125 and PROGRESS 179 said the memory "pays for a cache it destroys"; the
premium is real and the mechanism was wrong. Three things follow, and the third is the one that matters:

1. **The prompt total is now fully explained.** The memory arm's prompt was 4.6M tokens larger over 160
   episodes — 28.7k per episode, against 1,497 × 17 = 25.4k for a block present in every call. That is the
   block being **cached**, and it is what a correct bill looks like.
2. **The uncached premium is not.** 18.6k extra uncached tokens per episode against a first-call-only cost of
   1.5k. The block cannot produce twelve times its own size in misses while being cached, so something else
   does — and the two candidates are behavioural rather than positional: the memory arm's episodes fetch larger
   tool results, or its prefixes are re-read less often than the probe's cadence allows.
3. **The attribution was arithmetic over a population nobody checked.** PROGRESS 179 divided a job-level total
   by a call count and got a per-call premium. R93's own artefact records `calls: 1803` for the memory arm
   against the 2,667 that division used, so at least one of the two numbers is a different population than the
   sentence it appears in. That is the same class of defect as §34.126's empty pack: a number that is true of
   something, quoted about something else.

**The rule this adds.**

> A probe is an instrument and it fails like one — silently, in the direction of a confident answer. Warm the
> cache, isolate the shapes, and wait longer than the provider's write latency, or the verdict will be a
> measurement of your own dispatch order. Two of this probe's three runs produced a state that would have been
> written into a document as a finding.

## 34.128 R101 sent one prompt twice, and the difference is what a null looks like

R101's scaffold arm was built to price the wrapper: same agent, same tools, same tasks, a store
that declares itself empty. It ran (`43478128683`) and the pair read **−5.00pp** — 0.700 against
0.750, p = 0.7744, 7 tasks lost and 5 gained, 21 of 160 trials flipped.

The registered band was `[0.675, 0.775]`, and 0.700 is inside it, so the arm answered its question:
the wrapper costs five points, not the twenty-seven that would have made every earlier reading a
reading about the scaffold.

**But the two arms sent the same prompt.** `pack.filled` is 0 of 162 requests and `recall.served` is
0, because the agent's injection is guarded by `if pack:` and an empty store renders an empty string.
So the scaffold leg delivered the reference leg's prompt byte for byte, and the −5.00pp is a
**rerun of the same treatment**. That makes it the first *measured* null in this repository — the
MDE was always an estimate from a power calculation, and this is a point estimate from the thing
itself.

> Any paired delta below **5.0pp** at n = 40 is inside what two identical arms produce. The
> project's own history sits under that line: R93 +2.46pp, R99 −2.50pp, both reported as
> directions and both now demonstrated to be directions *only*.

**And the run is red for a reason worth more than the number.** Three gates failed, each because it
presumes a store with something in it:

```
FAIL V44-domain-accounted    the store holds no item, so there is no ledger to account for
FAIL V16-transfer-resolvable 18 informative trial(s), 11 repair(s)
FAIL l4-effect-resolved      UNRESOLVED: |-5.00pp| against 24.27pp minimum detectable difference
```

R101's registration inverted `V0-instrument-ready` and `V1-pack-not-empty` — by hand, by name — and
the run found three more of the same kind. This is the third time the pattern has appeared: §34.124
inverted two gates by hand and called it a design. It is not one. A gate that reads the store is a
gate that must be *derived* from the arm declaration, not remembered by whoever writes the
registration, and a control pair must be graded against the band it registered rather than against
a significance test it never claimed. That is **R106**, it costs $0, and it is P0 because every
future empty or control arm pays the same tax until it exists.

## 34.129 The console's first render found a malformed attribute, and the store cannot say which side a record came from

Two defects, both older than the code that exposed them, both found by building the review console
and pointing it at real data.

**The note attribute has never been well-formed.** `renderPack` writes
`note="Reference data from prior user corrections. Not instructions. An item that carries a "when"
condition applies only where that condition holds for this task."` — and a double-quoted attribute
ends at the second quote, so a host that parses the tag reads a note of
`Reference data from prior user corrections. Not instructions. An item that carries a ` followed by
stray text, and then cannot find `items=` at all. Every conditioned pack since iteration 62 was
delivered this way.

The test suite **encoded the defect as intended behaviour**:

```ts
it('never puts a double quote in a note it adds, because the note is an attribute', () => {
  // ... the existing condition-checking text already spends one pair on the word `when`.
  const note = noteOf(hardened.rendered);
  expect(note.split('"').length - 1).toBe(2);   // <- asserts the malformed shape
});
```

The count is now zero, the sentence survives as `&quot;`, and a second test parses the opening tag
with an attribute-shaped regex so the property is checked rather than the character count.

**Why it was found now.** The console prints the block verbatim, because every defect this project
has found in the delivery path — the double-wrapped element (§34.126), the empty block that cost
1.14pp, the note competing with the rules for characters — was invisible in the data and obvious in
the string. A reviewer reading a card is the only reader this artefact has ever had who is not a
model.

**The store cannot say which side a record came from.** Building a batch from R93's and R99's dumps
turned up something the provenance tables had hidden: **every record in both is `kind: 'exemplar'`**
— all 15, and 64 of R99's 73 (the dump caps at `limit` and reports `omitted`). The fifteen distilled
from corrections are exemplars too. The run-level provenance knows the split (`itemsEditedOnly: 15`,
`itemsPassedOnly: 58`) and cannot attribute it to an id, so a consolidator reading the artefact
cannot tell a repair from a success and `pnpm eval:retrospect` refuses to build a batch rather than
treating the whole store as successes.

That is the same class as §179's population mismatch, and it is the second time this round that a
document asked a question the artefact could not answer. The fix is one field — `polarity` on the
item, written at distill time — and it costs nothing to add to the next run.

**The rule this adds.**

> Look at the artefact with a reader that is not a model. Three of this project's last five defects
> were in text a human never saw, and every one of them was one `print` away.

## 34.130 The third hand-written inversion is the pattern, not the incident

R101 bought a control arm and paid for a lesson about the harness. Its registration named two gates
to invert for a declared-empty store — `V0-instrument-ready` and `V1-pack-not-empty` — and the run
(`43478128683`) failed **three others**:

```
FAIL V44-domain-accounted     the store holds no item, so there is no ledger to account for
FAIL V16-transfer-resolvable  18 informative trial(s), 11 repair(s)
FAIL l4-effect-resolved       UNRESOLVED: |-5.00pp| against 24.27pp minimum detectable difference
```

§34.124 had already inverted two gates by hand and called it a design. This is the third appearance
of one shape, and the shape is not "somebody forgot a gate": it is **a registration file enumerating
the gates that depend on its arm**, which is a second copy of the gate catalogue maintained by
whoever writes the registration. The copy drifts the first time a gate is added, and it drifts
silently, because a list of ids that is too short looks exactly like a list that is complete.

**Three dispositions were available, and only one survives.**

| disposition | what it makes the arm | why |
|---|---|---|
| waive the gate | unmeasurable | a gate that stands down for one arm is the vacuous pass this record keeps finding: `V6` and `V7` fire on an empty control list and certify nothing |
| omit the gate | silent | "this run is not graded" is the one statement a run whose pipeline matters most cannot make |
| **invert the gate** | **falsifiable** | the arm declared zero, so the quantity the gate requires to be non-zero is required to be zero instead |

Omission survives in exactly one case, and it is not a convenience: a gate whose **subject does not
exist** on the arm. `V16-transfer-resolvable` requires a hundred informative trials, and an arm that
served no rule has nothing to transfer — the eighteen trials it carried belong to the reference half
of the pair. There the honest sentence is "not graded, and here is why", and the omission travels in
`ScopedGates.omitted` so it is a row in the report rather than a silence.

**How the set is derived.** Each gate declares what it reads where it is built —
`storeReading`, `packGate`, `trialReading` — and the disposition of the whole set follows from the
arm's declaration. Twenty gates are marked: eleven read the store, five read the pack it fills, and
eight transfer gates exist only because a rule was served. A gate that reads a store and states no
empty form is **refused at grading time**, which is how the next gate somebody adds announces itself
instead of quietly becoming R101's fourth failure.

The declaration travels on the gate as a **non-enumerable symbol**, and that is the one subtle
decision here: an artefact is compared byte for byte by `eval:protocol`, so a marker that serialised
would have rewritten thirty-one committed reports to say something their runs never knew.
`JSON.stringify` cannot see it, `toEqual` cannot see it, and the published shape of a gate is exactly
what it was.

**Control pairs register a band, not a significance.** `l4-effect-resolved` asked R101's pair whether
it could resolve its own delta, and answered `24.27pp` — correct, and about a question the arm never
posed. A control pair withholds an interval before it runs: R101 registered `[−7.5, +2.5]pp` and read
−5.00pp, which is the arm agreeing with its own registration. When a band is present it **replaces**
the resolution question rather than sitting beside it; two conditions on one gate is how a gate stops
saying one thing. The band arrives as `TAU_BAND` from a repository variable, because `sota.yml`
already declares the twenty-five `workflow_dispatch` inputs GitHub will parse and a twenty-sixth makes
every dispatch in the repository unstartable — a limit `check-workflows.py` caught on the first push
of this change.

**Replayed against the run that found it.** The acceptance test is not the unit suite: R101's
artefact was downloaded from `43478128683` (`l4-evidence-none`, 20.6 MB) and the pair re-graded with the
new harness — `L4_FIRST=arms/reference/poc-l4.json`, `L4_SECOND=arms/memory/poc-l4.json`,
`TAU_BAND="-7.5,2.5"`. Before: `FAIL V44`, `FAIL V16`, `FAIL l4-effect-resolved`. After:

```
PASS V1-pack-not-empty     the pack carried 0.00 rule(s) per question; declared empty, so this must be 0 and is 0
PASS V32-fold-learning-intact  the fold read 0 learning row(s); declared empty, so this must be 0 and is 0
PASS V44-domain-accounted  the store holds 0 item(s); declared empty, so this must be 0 and is 0
PASS l4-effect-resolved    -5.00pp against the registered band [-7.50, 2.50]pp
```

Twelve gates pass, and the artefact carries five omissions with their reasons — `V6` ("an arm that
serves no pack has no pack-based control to hold to a rule") and the four transfer ids ("a transfer
trial presupposes a rule the arm served, and this arm declared it served none"). The line
`[l4-pair] verdict UNRESOLVED` still prints, and it should: that is `paired-verdict`'s statistical
sentence about the sample, not a gate about the arm. The distinction is the whole of §34.130 — the
pair could not resolve five points at n = 40, and that was never a defect in the arm.

**The rule this adds.**

> An exception a registration has to remember is a gate that will be forgotten. If a condition
> depends on what the arm is, the arm must be able to derive it — and a condition that cannot be
> derived must be refused, not skipped.

## 34.131 A model in the merge would have made R104 unreadable, and that is a measurement decision

The obvious objection to the retrospection design is that both systems it borrows from use a model to
merge. The premise is half true and the half that is false decides the design.

| system | who groups | who writes | merges *existing* memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALTK-Evolve | **cosine clustering** | a model, one guideline per cluster | yes — `support` conservation and `lossless`/`sup3` are deterministic dials |
| AutoGuide | none (context key retrieval) | a model, from a **contrastive trajectory pair** | **no** — first-order extraction, not second-order compression |
| ACE | embedding dedupe + id | Generator → Reflector → **Curator** | yes, and it measured the cost: **18,282 → 122 tokens, −9.6 points** |

So "they merge with a model" is two operations wearing one word — **a model writes** versus **a model
rewrites what is written**. Only the second is what this pipeline does, because its input is a store of
finished records rather than raw trajectories, and the only controlled measurement of it is ACE's
negative one.

Three arguments decide it here rather than merely favour it:

1. **Attribution.** R104 tests the *unit*. A model in the merge changes the grouping boundary and the
   prose together, so a positive delta could not be assigned to either — at n = 40, against a measured
   null of 5.00pp, one variable per arm is the budget.
2. **The ledger assumes stable text.** `applyDecision` refuses a decision whose `textBefore` no longer
   matches the card. Two model passes over one corpus produce two different cards, so a 3am session
   could not be replayed at 9am by anyone holding the same two files — and the audit trail *is* the
   state. A model can cross that boundary only by having its output snapshotted into the batch.
3. **The witness needs a baseline that cannot fail its own check.** The seed trigger is the
   intersection of its members' condition words, so it is entailed by construction and the gate grades
   the proposer rather than the fallback. A generated trigger is a guess that must clear the same gate,
   which is precisely what makes it a treatment.

**The model is registered rather than excluded.** `LlmInterpreter` already writes corrections with one,
and the deterministic proposal is the baseline a model-written one must beat — registered as **R104b**
at ≈ $0.01 per candidate against $1.21 for the arm it feeds. The better of the two remaining
entry points is the **splitter**, not the proposer: it moves the grouping and leaves the prose alone,
so ACE's failure mode does not apply to it.

**And the trigger for building it is a number.** `fragmentation` — the share of repairs no cluster
claims — is now computed by `clusterCensusOf` and carried on the batch as `census`. High fragmentation
with a high `witnessRate` means the bottleneck is grouping; low fragmentation with an unmoved R104 means
the unit was never the problem and the next arm is about abstention.

**The rule this adds.**

> Before adding a model to a compression stage, measure whether the stage's failure is *recall* or
> *fidelity*. A model fixes the first and damages the second, and the second is the one this pipeline
> was built to protect.

## 34.132 A field whose name contradicted its own comment, and the division that crossed populations

§179 attributed 99.9% of the memory arm's premium to the uncached column, and §181 found an error on the
way out: "R93's own artefact records `calls: 1803` for the memory arm; §179's division used 2,667." Both
numbers are real. They count different things:

| number | what it is | where it came from |
|---|---|---|
| **1,803** | the agent's **turns** | `diagnostics.agent_turns`, forwarded by the driver |
| **2,667** | **model calls** | the provider's own phase record, in the workflow log |
| **2,726** | the reference arm's model calls | same |

The field was `tau2.calls.calls`, and its docstring said, in the same file, "the episodes' calls belong
to the agent process, which reports a turn count rather than a call count". The name outranked the
sentence. A reader doing arithmetic on an artefact has no way to learn that the key is a label for the
wrong quantity — the artefact is the authority, and it was wrong about itself.

**Three repairs, none of which changes a published byte.** No committed report carries a τ² block, so
this was free: the key is `turns`, the provider's record is carried whole as `usage` (until now it
existed only in the workflow log, which is why a bill had to be divided by hand), and
`V8-call-reliability` states its population — `32/32 turns` on an episode tally, `32/32 calls` on a
distillation tally, because that client really does make model calls. The population travels as
`callPopulation` and defaults to `calls`, so every existing report re-renders identically.

**And the premium's decomposition, which the corrected population makes possible.** Five arms on one
table, per call, all at 160 conversations on the same 40 tasks:

```
R93 reference          408.0 uncached   (2,726 calls, 1,833 turns, no pack)
R101 reference         420.8 uncached   (2,716 calls, 1,806 turns, no pack)
R101 scaffold          413.7 uncached   (2,660 calls, 1,788 turns, empty pack, same agent class)
R93 memory           1,532.7 uncached   (2,667 calls, 1,803 turns, 1.1 items / 1,745 chars)
R99 memory           1,600.7 uncached   (2,646 calls, 1,788 turns, 1.3 items / 1,986 chars)
```

The wrapper costs **+5.7** tokens a call against the reference — 1.4% of the premium — and made 66 fewer calls: the agent class
this record blamed for two rounds costs nothing. The premium is therefore entirely the pack's
presence — and it splits in two: **+0.2819 tokens per served character** (one token per 3.55 characters,
i.e. exactly the price of re-billing the block) and a **flat 626.1–688.4 tokens a call** that does not move
with the pack's size at all.

**What that rules out.** The block is 436–499 tokens at 3.5–4.0 characters a token, so it is at most
**44%** of the 1,124.7-token premium even if every call paid for it in full. The majority is the arm's
own turn material, which means the mechanism is behavioural: a rule in the context changes the action
mix, and the action mix returns larger observations, which are uncached because they are new.

This is the third disposition of the same question, and the third to be decided against the obvious
repair:

| round | theory | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| R102.1 | the block sits outside the cached prefix | **refused by its own probe** — 31 uncached tokens a call in all three placements |
| §179 | the block is re-billed every call | **refuted here** — the size-dependent part is only 44% of the premium |
| §181 | something behavioural | **survives**, and is now instrumented rather than argued |

**The instrument, and why the lane did not have it.** `_record_usage` has held every call's `messages`
and the provider's `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` since the counter existed, and it summed both into totals
that cannot be divided by one another. It now aggregates a prompt census: characters of the material the
provider provably saw before this call (everything before the final two messages, since a tool loop
appends the assistant's call and the tool's result together), characters of the newest message, and a
characters-per-token ratio measured on the phase's **first call** — the only one the provider had never
cached, and therefore the only honest divisor. `prefix_coverage` is credited over provably-seen.

**The rule this adds.**

> A number and the population it was counted over are one fact, and a name that outlives its population
> is a number that will be divided wrongly. If a lane cannot see the population it is quoting, it must
> quote the one it can see — under that one's name.

## 34.133 The arm's switch was connected to nothing, and the same defect had already been fixed one layer up

R109 needed a knob on the wire. Asking whether the knob would arrive is the only reason this was found.

**Two disconnections, one arm.** The driver's `/v1/recall` facade — an in-process server the τ² agent
calls, not the HTTP package — read `task` and `text` from the query string and **discarded every other
pair**. Its callback was typed `(input: { task: string; text: string })`, so nothing downstream could
even see that a request had asked for something else. And the driver never read `TAU_PACK_MODE` in any
form, though the workflow sets it on both arms.

The consequence is not a missing feature. It is that **`MICROGLIA_PACK_KNOBS` could not change a pack**:
`eval:pack-knobs` renders a registration's mode into `anchoring=scope&minCoverage=0&limit=999&budget=200000`,
the Python agent appends it to the URL (PROGRESS 16195 verified the request carries seven query pairs),
and the process at the other end dropped all four. A `prefix` arm dispatched on this driver would have
served the **retrieved** pack — same selection, same budget, same items — and reported the prefix
protocol. The arm would have been its own control, with a registration, an artefact and a readback
attesting to a treatment that never ran.

**Why this is a repeat and not a novelty.** PROGRESS 16117 records the first instance: `/v1/recall` in
`packages/node` forwarded three of the five knobs it accepted, `minEvidence` and `anchoring` were
"described in the kernel's own type comments, honoured by `buildPack` and by the store, and unreachable
from the one surface every benchmark driver actually calls". The repair then was to hold the field list
once, in `recall-query.ts`, with the comment *"a sixth knob added to `RecallQuery` arrives as a compile
error in this file rather than as a silence on the wire."* That comment was true and insufficient: the
driver's facade was written beside it, not through it, and had its own field list — two names long.

**The rule this adds, which is a rule about comments.** *A file that says "this list is held once" is not
holding it once.* The claim has to be mechanically true, and the mechanism is that every caller parses
through the same function: `recall-query.ts` now lives in `kernel/`, the package both surfaces depend on,
and the driver's facade is a module with tests that start a real server on port 0 and assert what the
callback received. The test is the artifact that would have caught this; the comment was not.

**What it cost, and what it did not.** No committed artefact carries a pack mode, so no published number
is wrong — the prefix arm was registered and never dispatched. What the record loses is the belief that
its own switchboard was wired: an arm declared in a registration, a knob rendered by a resolver, a
fragment carried across three language boundaries and verified twice, and a handler that threw the last
one away. The verification stopped at the boundary that was being checked and the defect lived at the
boundary that was not.

**Second finding, smaller and the same shape.** `KnowledgePack.fold` is computed in both modes, so a
control arm's own support distribution is a number the artefact carries rather than a claim about a store
nobody looked at — and it is absent, not zero, on a host that cannot name a shape. The first version of
the census applied a group's union support to every member of the group, which reported `atLeastTwo: 2`
on a per-failure pack of two single-task records: the exact quantity the arm is measured on, inflated by
the arithmetic. Caught by the test that asserts the control arm reads `max: 1` — which exists because the
control's reading had to be a reading rather than an absence.

## 34.134 The readback refuses what the sentence beside it still prints

Three defects in one round, and they are the same defect in three layers. Each was found by writing the
test that asserts the *sentence* rather than the *value*, and none of them would have been caught by any
gate in the repository.

**1. A delta between two arms that delivered nothing.** `shapeArmReading` computed its contrasts and then
computed its state. The state is what decides whether a run reports a contribution, and the state is
computed from the arms — not from the contrasts — so the order was free to be wrong, and it was: a
`NO_DELIVERY` run has two arms with identical task rows, so `compareArms` returned a perfectly well-formed
`0.00pp [0.00, 0.00] p=1.0000` over four paired tasks. The artefact that carried it also carried
`state: "NO_DELIVERY"`, which says in the same document that nothing was delivered. Every reader downstream
— the readback, the summary line, the appendix someone writes six weeks later — would have taken the delta
and ignored the state, which is exactly the failure mode `readNotedFacadeArtifact` was built to prevent one
document over. The fix is ordering, and the comment beside it says why the order is not cosmetic.

**2. The note arm had already shipped it.** `readNotedFacadeArtifact` has refused a contrast in
`IDENTITY_BROKEN` and `NO_DELIVERY` since the day it was written — `contrasts: []` in both states, with a
comment about a defaulted readback being how a run that never measured becomes a result. The **summary
line** did not: `noteFacadeSummary` mapped `reading.contrasts` without asking the state, so the one line the
workflow prints into the job summary carried `standard vs none 0.00pp [0.00, 0.00] p=1.0000` under the
words `IDENTITY_BROKEN:`. A refusal that lives in the typed reader and not in the prose beside it is half a
refusal, and the half that survives is the half a human reads. Fixed, and the test asserts the absence of
the clause rather than the presence of the state.

**3. The control compared the wrong arm to itself.** The containment assertion is
`control.ids.length − treatment.folded === treatment.ids.length`. The first version read
`control.ids.length − control.folded`, and the control never folds: the equation collapsed to `n === n`,
which is true for every pack the fold shortened and for several it did not. It is worth stating plainly
because the test that caught it looks trivial — a three-item control against a two-item treatment whose
fold reports nothing — and the assertion it protects is the one that makes the whole arm a comparison
rather than two experiments. A control whose arithmetic is an identity is not a control; it is a comment
with a return type.

**What the three have in common, and the rule this adds.** In each case the *typed* path was right and the
*adjacent* path was not: the readback refused and the summary printed; the state was computed and the
contrast was not gated on it; the equation had the right shape and the wrong operand. This repository's
gates read artefacts and diff protocols, and none of them reads a sentence. So the rule is: **when a
refusal exists in a reader, the line derived from that reader must be asserted too**, and the assertion has
to be about the absence — `not.toContain('vs standard')` — because a presence assertion passes on the
wrong state. That is cheap, it is testable offline, and it is the only mechanism that catches a display
layer disagreeing with the rule it displays.

**Cost of finding them:** $0. All three were caught by unit tests over pure functions before any dispatch
was queued, which is the ordering this record keeps asking for and rarely gets: R70's coverage gate refused
a paid run, and these three would have been paid runs too.

## 34.135 The side was guessed from a field that carries no side, and the guess had a sign

**What was measured.** `pnpm eval:retrospect` is the runner that turns a store into a review batch: it
classifies each record as a `repair` (usable for writing a guideline) or a `pass` (usable only to
contradict one), then clusters the repairs. It could not run on a single artefact this lane has produced.
The reason was recorded as an instrumentation gap in §34.129 — the dumps carry no per-item side — and the
gap was real. What was not recorded is that the fallback standing in for it was **worse than the gap**.

```ts
function outcomeOf(item: StoreItem): 'repair' | 'pass' {
  if (item.polarity === 'repair' || item.polarity === 'pass') return item.polarity;
  return item.kind === 'exemplar' || item.kind === 'procedure' ? 'pass' : 'repair';
}
```

`kind` is what the distiller's model chose to write, not which half of a run the record came from. The τ²
distiller writes `exemplar` for a correction and for a success alike — all 15 of R93's records and 64 of
R99's are exemplars, the fifteen from corrections included — so the fallback read **every real record as a
success**. A random fallback would have produced a mixed corpus and a batch whose proposal quality could
be argued about; this one produced a refusal, and that is what made it look like a missing instrument
rather than a wrong one.

**The failure mode it was one edit away from.** The refusal sentence said two causes and could not tell
them apart:

> `the store holds 15 record(s) and none of them is a repair (kinds: exemplar); nothing to consolidate.
> Either the run distilled only successes, or the dump carries no per-item polarity and every record reads
> as one`

The obvious repair — "then let the fallback decide" — would have consolidated fifteen corrections into
guidelines *labelled as successes*, under the name of a lane whose entire premise is that a success may not
teach a guideline. That is the laundering R99 already paid 6.5 points for, arriving through a default.

**Why no test caught it.** `vitest.config.ts` excludes `**/bin/**`, on the argument that a CLI is a shell
over logic that lives in the package. The only function in the repository that decides whether a real
artefact can be read was inside that shell, so it had no test at all — not an untested branch, an
untested decision. The exclusion is right and its precondition was not met: `bin/` may hold a shell, and
this one held the reader. The logic is now `packages/eval/src/retrospect-store.ts` (23 tests,
100/100/100/100) and the shell is a shell.

**And the fallback was deleted rather than repaired**, because the two candidates differ in kind. A
`repair`/`pass` default is a *semantic* decision about one record's provenance, which no enum can carry;
what the reader does instead is count the records it cannot classify and refuse when that leaves the
corpus empty, naming which of the two causes fired. A silence that is counted is an instrument; a silence
that is filled in is a guess.

**A second, quieter instance of the same shape is in the replacement.** The new field is checked against
the run-level census that already existed (`provenance.itemsEditedOnly` / `itemsPassedOnly` /
`itemsMixed`, joined through `EvidenceRef.runId`), and for a fully labelled store the two agree **by
construction** — the field's two populations and the census's three both partition the item count. Written
as `agree when the numbers match`, the check would have certified nothing while looking like evidence.
What it actually tests is the inequality (the store may not record fewer repairs than the join knows
about, which is what a wrong `polarityFor` mapping produces) and the count (a truncated sample or a
mismatched artefact). The module says so at the top, and the state is `unavailable` — not `agree` — when
the comparison cannot run.

**The rule this adds.**

> A default that maps an enum onto a semantic decision must be checked against the population that
> exists, not against the enum's other members. Here the population was one value wide and the default
> covered it entirely.

**Cost of finding it:** $0, and it was found by running the pipeline on a real artefact and reading the
sentence it printed — the same reader that found §34.129.

## 34.136 A failed run deleted its own evidence, and the summary named a cause nobody had observed

**What happened.** R104's first dispatch (`43578774040`) produced no measurement: 74 learn episodes,
fifteen corrections, fifteen empty replies from the distiller, zero candidates, zero stored. The
driver stopped before the evaluation half, which is the correct behaviour. The artefacts it left were
a three-line stub and a job log, and between them they could not answer a single follow-up question.

The stub:

```json
{ "id": "poc-l4", "title": "… (no measurement: the run stopped before any task was scored)",
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash", "n": 0, "calls": 0,
  "metrics": { "status_no_measurement": 1, … },
  "notes": ["The run stopped before any task was scored: 15 correction(s) -> 15 asked -> 0 candidate(s)
             -> 0 admitted -> 0 stored -> 0 servable (0 refused, 0 failed): the interpreter answered all
             15 event(s) with no claim of its own: nothing was thrown away after the reply, so the
             model is what carried nothing", …] }
```

**Why that is the wrong shape for this class.** A no-measurement record is the one file in the lane
with no result in it, so its whole value is diagnostic — and it was the only artefact class that
carried no diagnostics. A successful arm's file carries the funnel, the reply census, the store
census, the shape supply, the population switch, the unit, the form and the distilled population. The
stopped arm's carried the sentence that summarised all of them. So "could this arm have measured
anything even with a distiller that worked?" — a question the shape supply answers at $0 — could only
be answered by buying the learn half again.

**The second defect is the same class one layer out.** The workflow step that exists to announce a
stop printed, for **any** `status_no_measurement`:

> L4 stopped before measuring: the provider failed its pre-flight probe

The probe was off. The endpoint had answered 1,233 calls with a 90.2% cache hit. The failure was in
the distiller, and the annotation named a subsystem the run had not exercised. An artefact whose
content is a diagnosis was annotated with a sentence its own driver had contradicted — and the
annotation is what a human reads first, in the run list, without opening anything.

**Why no test caught it.** Both are write-path shape, not logic: `noMeasurement()` had no field to
put diagnostics in, so the driver had nowhere to hand them over even though it had computed them
(§34.132's pattern, third instance). The fix is a field on the marker plus one spread in `l4.ts`, and
the test is at the process boundary the field crosses — a stand-in driver that raises a refusal
carrying a census, and an assertion that the census is in the file. The warning is fixed by not
guessing: it prints the driver's first note verbatim and appends the funnel, the reply census and the
shape supply to the step summary when they are present.

**The rule this adds.**

> An artefact that records a failure must carry what the failure was observed through. A sentence
> summarising five counts is a claim about evidence; the evidence itself costs bytes and cannot be
> recovered after the process exits.

**Cost of finding it:** $0.1875 of learn episodes, of which the informative part was the fifteen
replies — and those were discarded.

## 34.137 The arm quoted a store census and did not pin the switch that produces it

**What was registered.** R104's premise, quoted from R99:

> 73 corrections distilled into **53 action shapes**, of which **10 are taught by two tasks and 5 by
> three**.

**What was dispatched.** `distillScope` was not in R104's header. The dispatch read
`vars.TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE`, which was empty, and `resolveDistillScope` treats empty as its default:
`edited`. The learn half produced **fifteen** corrections, from the fifteen tasks that failed out of
seventy-four. The funnel's own first number says so: `15 correction(s)`.

**Why that is not a detail.** A fold needs two tasks behind one routine, and the count of routines
that have them is a property of the population: R99's 73 records collapsed to 53 shapes with ten at
support ≥2. Fifteen records cannot contain ten corroborated routines; at R99's own ratio the expected
count is about one. The arm's treatment is the fold, so **the dispatched arm could not have measured
the claim it registered whatever the distiller had done** — and the fifteen empty replies, which are
the reason the run is being discussed at all, are a second, independent reason it produced nothing.

**Why the header had no rule against it.** Eight switches are already refused when a registration
leaves them to a variable: the floor, the pair, the note levels, the pack units, the form, the unit,
the pack mode and the pack shape. Each was added after an arm published one treatment under another's
name. The population was the eighth and the omission was structural rather than accidental: the switch
arrived in R62 for a different question ("should a store learn from successes too?"), and no round
before this one had a treatment whose *supply* was the population.

**What changed, and what did not.** The header pins `distillScope: all`, and `prereg.ts` now refuses a
`two-unit` arm that does not. The amendment is recorded inside the registration with the reason and
the run id, and it is legitimate *because there is no measurement to amend*: the first dispatch
produced no `pass^4`, no delta and no store, so the predictions and refutations are the ones that were
registered, unchanged. A registration amended after a reading would be a different act entirely, and
the note says which one this was.

**The rule this adds.**

> A registration that quotes a measurement must pin the switch that produced it. A census in a premise
> is a claim about a population, and a population inherited from a variable is a premise nobody
> declared.

**Cost of finding it:** $0 to reason about, $0.1875 to have had the chance — and it would have cost a
second learn half to notice without the first fix in §34.136.

## 34.138 The reflector was the actor, and nothing said so

**The coupling.** The driver builds its distiller with:

```ts
model:
  process.env["TAU_DISTILL_MODEL"]?.trim() ||
  process.env["TAU_MODEL"] ||
  "deepseek-chat",
```

`TAU_DISTILL_MODEL` is empty in every dispatch this lane has ever run, so the model that **writes the
memory** is whichever model **acts**, silently and always. That was invisible for as long as the two were
deliberately the same: R93's and R99's stores were written by `deepseek-flash` because the agent was
`deepseek-flash`. When R101 changed the agent's model for a decomposition leg, it changed the reflector too,
and no registration declared it, no artefact recorded it, and no gate could see it — the same shape as
§34.133's switch connected to nothing, one layer further out.

**Why it matters beyond bookkeeping.** The two roles are not the same job. ACE's own architecture separates
them (a Reflector that distils, a Curator that merges) and its ablations credit the Reflector with a
substantial share of the gain; the label-free self-improvement literature finds that a reflector below a
capability threshold does not produce a worse lesson but **none**, and the small-model self-restatement work
puts that threshold at a size where "restate what this correction teaches" is a task a model can fail
completely. So the lane's one observed total failure — fifteen corrections, fifteen empty replies — is a
*predicted* failure of a small reflector, arriving through a default nobody had reason to look at.

**What was fixed, and what was not.** The artefact now names the writer (`distillModel`, on every arm), and
a pre-flight asks one fixture correction before the learn half is bought, so "the writer produced nothing"
costs one call instead of 74 episodes. The *choice* of writer is left where it belongs: it is a treatment,
it changes the store, and a registration has to declare it rather than inherit it. That decision needs the
pre-flight's answer first, which is the next dispatch's job, not this iteration's.

**The rule this adds.**

> A default that binds two roles to one value must be visible in the record it produces. Here the roles were
> a writer and an actor; the default was invisible for eight rounds because for eight rounds the two were
> deliberately identical, and it became a variable the moment one of them moved.

**Cost of finding it:** $0 — the code was three lines and the artefact already carried the wrong model's
name in a field nobody read.

## 34.139 Two fields, one writer, and two meanings for silence

**The coupling.** `distill` writes both `scope` and `polarity` from one candidate in one call, and the
two fields answer the same kind of question — *what does it mean that this value is not here?* — in
opposite ways:

| field | absent means | where it is decided |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `polarity` | **unclassified**: counted, never filled in, and a store of unlabelled records is refused rather than read as successes | `readStoreDump`, written in R110 after a fallback read every τ² record as a pass |
| a `scope` dimension | **wildcard**: the rule matches every request on that dimension | `scopeMatches`, which is permissive on purpose |

Both are defensible alone. `scopeMatches` has to be permissive or a store written from a handful of
examples serves nothing, and `polarity` has to be strict or a consolidator reads guesses as evidence.
Together they are a trap for the one reader who arrives without knowing which field he is holding,
and the glossary's `Scope` entry — six paragraphs of dimensions and no sentence about absence — sent
him to the wrong answer with a clear conscience.

**The second defect was arithmetic.** The artefact's sample projected an item's scope to `domain` and
dropped the other four dimensions, so the population this record has spent eleven iterations arguing
about was never in any artefact to be counted. The schema had six dimensions; the record carried one;
no reader could tell a store where nobody declared a field from a projection that discarded it.

**What was fixed.** The projection carries what it reads, states which dimensions it carried
(`scopeDims`), and the census refuses when the statement is missing. `universalityCensus` counts the
record that has neither bound — no `when`, no optional dimension — which is the object the 2026
memory-harm results measure, and it counts records the dump cannot place separately rather than
folding them into the intersection.

**The rule this adds.**

> A field whose absence is load-bearing must say what its absence means, and two fields written by one
> writer in one call must either agree about silence or state why they differ. The failure is not that
> `scope` is permissive; it is that nothing anywhere said so, and the artefact could not be asked.

## 34.140 A zero that belonged to the unit, read as a failure of the distiller

**What was written, and when it was wrong.** §PROGRESS 190 first reported R99's store as

> `store.conditioned 0, unconditioned 73` — **every record states no condition**, and eleven iterations
> read that count as a retrieval statistic rather than as a statement about what a rule *is*.

and drew from it that the distiller never writes a condition. Six hours later the same artefact was read
for a different field:

```
distillUnit  { unit: 'raw', traces: 0, traced: 0, claims: 73 }
distillForm  { form: 'record', refused: 0, maxTokens: 1200 }
rawlog       { records: 73, clipped: 9, toolBan: false, ceiling: 2000 }
```

The store was written by the **raw** unit, whose record is `Q: … / A: …` copied from the episode.
`rawLogInterpreter` has no `when` to write, so `conditioned: 0` is the unit's definition and not a
distiller that declined to state a condition. The llm forms require one (`TRACE_RULES`: *"it must be
checkable on a different request and must not hold for every request"*), and R111's evidence is that on
this model they return nothing at all — which is why the lane runs `raw` in the first place.

**The shape of the error is the one this record has already paid for twice.** R110 deleted a fallback
that read a `kind` for a side; that was inferring a **semantic** from a field's default. This is its
mirror: inferring a **failure** from a counter's zero, in an artefact that carried the field explaining
the zero two keys away. Both are readings of a silence, and in both cases the document said what the
silence was to anyone who read the whole of it.

**What survived the correction.** The population is still real — 73 records, none conditional, 0.625
against R93's fifteen at 0.700 — but the *cause* moved from "the writer will not write a condition" to
"the lane selected a unit that has none", and the arm that follows is a paired comparison of the two
units holding the population fixed (**R113a**), not a prompt repair.

**The rule this adds.**

> A counter reports a property of the unit it was taken in. Before a zero is read as a defect, the same
> document must be asked which unit produced it — and when the document answers, the answer belongs in
> the sentence that quotes the zero.

## 34.141 The two ends of the axis were the same unit, and the axis was the population

**What was written, and what the second artefact said.** §PROGRESS 190 corrected a zero (34.140) and
reported the lane's two stores as differing "in form *and* size at once" — R99's seventy-three records
against R93's fifteen. Both artefacts were then read for the unit that wrote them:

```
R93  run 43436606915  distillUnit {unit:'raw', claims:15}   distillScope 'edited'  conditioned 0  clipped 3  pass^4 0.700
R99  run 43463317323  distillUnit {unit:'raw', claims:73}   distillScope 'all'     conditioned 0  clipped 9  pass^4 0.625
```

`unit: 'raw'` both times. The form is identical, so the seven and a half points are the price of
**fifty-eight more raw records** and not of a different kind of record. The corrected sentence is
narrower and it points somewhere else.

**Why the error was easy and why it mattered.** `R93` and `R99` are described in this record by what they
tested — a paired arm, a supply arm — and neither description names the unit, because when both arms ran
the unit was a constant nobody had a reason to read. A constant is invisible in the same way a default is
invisible (34.138): it becomes a variable only when something changes, and nothing had changed since the
lane fell back to `raw`.

**What the pair now explains.** `correction` is the default unit, and its prompt makes `when` mandatory:

> `when` is the condition under which the account generalises to a different question … It must be
> checkable against the schema and the question, and it must not hold for every question.

R111 measured what that unit returns on this backend: fifteen corrections, fifteen empty replies. So the
lane's store shape is downstream of its writer's capability — a writer that cannot abstract leaves only
the unit that copies, a copy has no condition because it is a copy, and copies get worse as they multiply.
Every store-side arm since R85 has been tuning that consequence.

**The rule this adds.**

> When two arms differ in a metric and share an unread constant, the metric belongs to the constant until
> the constant is read. Here the constant was the distillation unit, and reading it turned a comparison of
> forms into a comparison of sizes — which is the comparison R99 had already made and closed.

## 34.142 A census that counted one silence and rejected the other, on the argument that someone else had it

**What the module said.** R111's `replyCensus` classified a reply as `empty` when it parsed to a
candidate list of length zero, and left every other failure to the interpreter:

> A reply that is not JSON is **not** counted as empty: it is the interpreter's error to count, it
> carries its own sample, and folding it into "the model said nothing" is the conflation this census
> exists to end.

**What the run printed.**

```
[tau2] distill replies: 73 call(s), 0 empty, 6824 character(s) returned
[tau2] learn: … 63 answered by the rule fallback, reasons MG_E_INVALID_SIGNAL=63
[tau2] distill fault MG_E_INVALID_SIGNAL: LLM response is not JSON <- 
```

`0 empty` is a healthy line. Sixty-three of seventy-three replies produced no claim. The proof the
delegation rested on — "it carries its own sample" — was the arrow at the end of the third line,
pointing at nothing.

**Why it pointed at nothing.** `parseCandidates` set `preview: text.slice(0, 160)` on `text =
raw.trim()`. A reply of whitespace trims to `''`, so the preview was `''`, and `sampleOf` rendered
`<- ${''}`. The parser was not wrong about the category; it was asked to quote a reply that had no
characters to quote, and the census had already decided that this category was somebody else's.

**Three properties the fix holds.**

1. `blank` is classified **before** the parse, because the parser's verdict on an empty string
   (`not JSON`) describes a text that was never there. A silent model and a model that answered in
   prose have different fixes and now have different states.
2. The four states are a **partition**: `answered + empty + blank + unparsed === calls`, asserted.
   A count that does not add up is how the first version hid a 63-event population behind `0`.
3. An error's `preview` is **never** empty: `replyPreview` returns `the reply held no visible
   character (N whitespace character(s))` for whitespace and `the reply was empty (0 characters)`
   for `''`. The N matters: a model that spent a completion budget returning four newlines is a
   different fault from one that returned nothing.

**The generalisation.** The delegation was sound in principle — an interpreter's error is the right
place to sample a parse failure — and it failed because the delegate's field was empty in exactly
the case the delegator declined to count. A census may delegate a *sample*; it may not delegate the
*count*, because the delegate is the thing under test.

## 34.143 The one state that can measure the noise was the one state that refused to compute

**What the module did.** R109a's shape arm computes a paired contrast between the two pack units, and
returns before computing it in every state that is not `MEASURED`:

> The contrasts are computed **after** the state, because two of the four states report no
> contribution: a dispatch whose facades served no pack has two arms with identical task rows, so a
> contrast computed before the state would carry `0.00pp [0.00, 0.00]`.

That reasoning is correct for `NO_DELIVERY` and `CONTAINMENT_BROKEN`, and it was applied to
`NO_TREATMENT` by association. R104 ran it:

```
NO_TREATMENT: per-failure pass4 55.00% served 164/164 items/req 5.000 chars/req 2102 folded 0
            | collapse pass4 72.50% served 162/162 items/req 5.000 chars/req 2100 folded 0
```

**The state is not the same kind of state.** `NO_TREATMENT` means the fold removed nothing, so both
facades rendered the *same* pack from the *same* store over the *same* split. The two arms are two
evaluations of one configuration, and their difference is not a contribution — it is the lane's
run-to-run spread, which is the floor every other contrast on the board has to clear. Refusing to
compute it left a reader with two numbers side by side under a label that forbids subtracting them.

**The fix keeps the refusal and adds the arithmetic.** `nullContrasts` is computed only in
`NO_TREATMENT`, is never merged into `contrasts`, and the summary prints it with the sentence that
says what it is:

> the fold removed nothing, so the two arms are one treatment: this delta is the lane's run-to-run
> noise at n=40, and no arm here may claim an effect smaller than it

`NO_DELIVERY` and `CONTAINMENT_BROKEN` still report nothing, for the reason the original comment
gave — those pairs are degenerate, and a delta between two arms that never delivered is a number
about the arithmetic rather than about the run.

**The rule this adds.**

> A state that invalidates a comparison must say which part it invalidates. "No treatment" removes
> the *attribution* and leaves the *measurement*; folding the two together discards the only free
> estimate of the resolution every other result is judged against.

## 34.144 A workflow step is logic that no test can reach, and this one had never run

**What happened.** R111 put the "say so when nothing was measured" decision inline, as a
`node -e "…"` string in `sota.yml`. R104 executed it for the first time on a run that measured
nothing — the case it exists for — and it failed:

```
[eval]:9
    // The sentence here used to read the
SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input
```

Line 9 is a comment quoting the old warning: `// The sentence here used to read "the provider failed
its pre-flight probe" for every`. The double quotes inside it closed the shell's own `"` string, so
the script ended at the comment and bash concatenated the rest as unquoted text.

**Why it had never run.** Every dispatch before R104 either measured (the step printed nothing) or
stopped before the step was reached. A branch that only executes on failure is exercised only by
failures, and the first failure is the wrong time to discover that it does not parse.

**The shape of the fix is the point, not the escaping.** The decision is `noMeasurementNote`, a pure
function over the artefact, with tests for a missing artefact, a missing reason, a **blank** reason,
a missing metrics block, and the two not-run causes. The workflow calls
`pnpm eval:say-what-happened`. Two properties come with it: the reason can never print as an empty
string after a colon, and the section carries the writer before the funnel, because a dispatch that
measured nothing still knows who wrote its store.

**The rule this adds.**

> Logic in a workflow file is logic no coverage instrument reaches and no test can call. If a step
