> has to decide something, the decision belongs in the package — the step's job is to call it.

## 34.145 The counts were in the artefact, under a key this audit had not opened

**What §PROGRESS 191 first said.**

> | D4 | the artefact carried no fault counts at all | 63 fallbacks existed only in the log |

**What the artefact says.**

```json
"learning": {
  "rows": 74, "unanswered": 0, "edited": 15, "distilled": 6, "distillFailed": 0,
  "candidates": 16, "events": 73, "llmFailed": 63,
  "llmFailedReasons": { "MG_E_INVALID_SIGNAL": 63 },
  "llmFailedSamples": { "MG_E_INVALID_SIGNAL": "MG_E_INVALID_SIGNAL: LLM response is not JSON <- " },
  "dropped": {}
}
```

Every count was there, including the fault histogram and one sample — and the sample is the dangling
arrow, in the document, not only in the log. The claim was false and it was written before the block
was opened, because the earlier read had looked at `tau2.distillReplies` and `tau2.funnel` and
concluded that a field which was not in those two was not in the file.

**What is actually missing, and it is narrower.** `llmFailed` counts events the model threw on. It
does not say how many of those the fallback answered, how many claims the fallback produced, or which
side the stored claims came from — and on this run the answer to all three is the same and is the one
that matters: 63 invocations, 63 answers, **0 claims**, so the store is the model's. `distillFaults`
and `distillWriter` add those; they do not add counts that were already published.

**The rule this adds.**

> An absence claim is a claim about a document, and it has to be checked against the whole document.
> "The field is not where I looked" and "the field is not there" are different findings, and the
> first one is not a finding at all.

This is the fifth reading of a silence in two iterations — the `kind` fallback (34.135), the scope
dimension (34.139), the `conditioned` zero (34.140), the unread constant (34.141), and now a block
that was read as missing. The first four were wrong about **code**; this one was wrong about **a
file**, which is worse, because a file is the thing the next reader trusts.

## 34.146 A regime is a property of a run, not of the provider's default

**What the code did.** The τ² driver built its distillation client without a `thinking` parameter, and
the comment beside the token ceiling said:

> The coupling to a thinking regime is not wired here because this lane's distiller never thinks —
> `TAU_THINKING` reaches the Python half, and this process's own client sends no reasoning parameter.

The second clause is a fact about the code. The first clause is a claim about the run, and it does not
follow: a client that sends no parameter receives the endpoint's **default**, which this lane never
chose and never recorded. The BIRD lane has passed `thinking` through `LlmClient` since R84, where the
same family of failure cost **572 of 1,400 replies** and a validity gate caught it; the τ² lane is the
only client in the package that left the decision to somebody else.

**What it cost.** R104: 73 distillation calls, **63 replies with no visible character**, 16 candidates
from ten answers, six records stored, five of them served to every request. The artefact could not say
whether the model had spent its budget thinking, because the distillation client's token census was
not recorded anywhere — the `usage` block belongs to τ²'s Python half.

**What changed.** One `distillClient()` factory, used by the pre-flight and the arm, sending
`thinking: 'off'`; and `distillClient` on the artefact carrying calls, prompts, failures, retries,
tokens and `reasoningTokens`. The ceiling did not change, because with the regime stated 1,200 tokens
is four times the reply the schema keeps — `distillBudget` remains the function for the lane that does
think.

**The rule this adds.**

> A parameter a client does not send is a parameter the provider chooses. Any comment that asserts the
> resulting behaviour has to name the mechanism that enforces it, and where the mechanism is absent
> the sentence is a hope rather than a description.

The corollary is about artefacts: a run cannot be re-read for a quantity it never recorded. The
distillation client's tokens were absent from every artefact this lane wrote, so "the replies were
blank" was a fact and "the model thought instead of answering" was a hypothesis no committed document
could settle.

## 34.147 The answer was in the file, and the read-back stopped at the funnel: six claims of pure format and 0 of 667 entities

**What was concluded.** §34.145 §191 both read R104's artefact as far as the funnel — `73 asked, 16
candidates, 6 stored, 63 faults` — and drew the two findings that line supports: the model answered 10
of 73 events, and the store covered 14% of its population. Both are true. §191 then wrote R112's premise
on top of them: *which writer can write*, on the reading that a claim without a `when` is not an answer.

**What the file also contained, unopened.** Four blocks in the same 100 KB artefact:

- `storeItems.items` — the **full text of all six stored claims**, with their `when`, `kind`, `scope`
  and `supportTasks`.
- `faithfulness` — `corrections 71, entities 667, kept 0, whole 0, redacted 9`.
- `coverage` — per-pair coverage over the 820 injected (request, item) pairs: median 4.76%, 195 pairs
  at zero.
- `served.byItem` — how many of the 164 requests each of the six items reached: 152, 130, 48, 164, 164,
  162.
- `pack.droppedForSize: 164` — an item dropped for size on **every** request.

**And the premise was refuted by a fifth field that *was* quoted.** `store` reads
`conditioned: 5, unconditioned: 1`. Five of six claims carry a condition. `when` is not the bottleneck;
it never was. §191 quoted the field and read past it, because the sentence it was writing ("the
artefact could not say whether a claim carried a condition") was about the funnel's census rather than
about the store's.

**What the six claims say.** Every one is a fact about the wire format or the call order: the JSON shape
of an action (`name`+`arguments`), the names of two arguments (`item_ids`, `new_item_ids`), which
argument a return carries that a cancellation does not (`payment_method_id` vs `reason`), the
representation choice, and twice an ordering rule. None states **what a request of a given shape
requires** — the only kind of claim that could change an answer.

**Why, arithmetically.** `distillForm` carries `refused: 10` beside `16 claims`. The tool-name ban
refuses any candidate that names one of the fourteen tools this split learned from. The six survivors
name no tool — they say "the address update action" — and the ten refusals are the candidates that said
which operation applies. So the ban removed the operational half and left the schema half.

> **A treatment that removes the knowledge it exists to make transferable.** The ban is right in
> principle: a claim that names `modify_pending_order_address` cannot transfer to an unseen scenario.
> The defect is that nothing measured what survives it, and what survives is the residue a schema
> validator already knows — 4.8% median coverage, 0% entity survival, 23.8% of injected pairs matching
> nothing.

**The rule this adds.**

> Reading an artefact is not the same as reading its summary block. Every iteration that ends at the
> funnel's last line has to say which blocks it did **not** open, because a hundred kilobytes of
> committed evidence is cheap to re-read and the alternative is paying for the next arm to learn a
> number that was already on disk.

**The falsifier.** If a `(model, form)` pair produces a claim that names no tool **and** states an
operational condition, the residue is not a property of the ban and this reading is wrong. `eval:writer-probe`
is the instrument that can produce one, and its `no-writer` verdict is a result rather than a failure.

## 34.148 An audit that hid its own subject, a denominator four times too generous, and a parameter nobody sent

Three defects, and the third is the one that cost a whole benchmark.

### The 86% that a missing parameter cost

R104 asked a distiller about 73 corrections and recorded 10 answers. Three iterations were spent
excluding explanations — the parser (`distill-replies.ts`, four states), the writer (R112, 8 of 8
candidate pairs answer), the `when` field (`store.conditioned: 5`, quoted in §191 and read past).
R118 then ran the same 73 corrections with **one change**: `thinking: 'off'` stated by the client
instead of left to the endpoint's default.

```
              calls  answered  blank  candidates  stored   chars
R104             73        10     63          16       6    6,824
R118             73        73      0         143      86   67,859
```

**The default for this model is to think, thinking is billed at the output rate, and it is taken out
of the same 1,200-token ceiling the reply needs.** A reply that spends its ceiling reasoning is a
reply with no content, and that is indistinguishable from a model that declines — which is why it
took four iterations of instrumenting the reply to find a cause that was in the request.

> **An omitted parameter is not a neutral default.** Every client in this project now states its
> regime. `distillClient` is one factory so the pre-flight and the arm cannot ask under two
> regimes, and the artefact carries `reasoningTokens` so the next dispatch can tell a budget from a
> refusal in one jump.

### The audit whose selector excluded the lane it audits

`poc-power-audit.json` exists to put every published delta beside the difference its sample could
have resolved. Its scan required a `per_case` array. The τ² lane writes
`comparison {paired, lost, gained, deltaPp}`, because the τ² agent owns its own questions and
reports totals rather than per-question outcomes.

So `poc-l4-pair.json` was committed, cited in §191 and in Appendix AK, and **not in the audit**. Its
row reads delta +1.47pp against a **21.41pp** floor — four and a half times coarser than the loosest
BIRD row the audit was reporting, and the only row that governs whether this project's SOTA statement
can be ordered against anything.

> **A filter that selects by shape inherits the blindness of the shape it guessed.** The audit now
> reads both shapes, prefers `per_case` when a file has both because a summary must not become the
> evidence, and distinguishes "not a pair" (`null`) from "claims to be a pair and is not" (an error).

Two further pieces of that fix exist because the first version was wrong:

- **The direction check.** `gained` means the treatment won. A file that recorded its two sides the
  other way round still yields a row, with the opposite sign, and nothing downstream would notice.
  The reader refuses a file whose own `deltaPp` disagrees with `gained − lost` by more than 0.01pp.
- **Where the check lives.** It was written in `power-audit.ts` first. The next edit to that file
  deleted the guard that skips unpaired files and **no test noticed**, because the command has no
  test. Selector and reader moved into `power.ts`; the command now holds no decisions at all.

### The denominator that was four times too generous

`effectClaimPp` refuses a registration whose claimed effect its own sample could not have resolved.
The first draft computed the floor from `sample`. On this record `sample` is **episodes**, and a
pairing is one per **task**: `poc-l4-pair.json` reads `paired: 68` for a dispatch whose registration
says `sample: 272`.

| read as | floor at 68 tasks | floor over 272 episodes |
|---|---|---|
| complete discordance | **33.98pp** | 16.99pp |
| the discordance the last pairing showed | 21.41pp | 10.70pp |

The arithmetic was right both times and the denominator was wrong once, in the direction that makes
a gate **pass** claims its own design cannot see. It now reads `testTasks` when a header states one
and `sample` otherwise, which is correct for both lanes: a BIRD question and a BIRD task are the same
thing, which is why no BIRD header has the field.

The same field's first draft also imported `detectableDelta` from `protocol.ts`, which imports the
core package — and `prereg.ts` runs **before anything is built**, a constraint its own test enforces
by walking the import closure. The formula moved to `detectable.ts`, which imports nothing, and is
re-exported from `protocol.ts` so no caller changed. Two copies of one formula would have been worse
than the dependency.

**The rule this adds.**

> A gate's denominator has to be the unit the measurement is in, and the unit is not always the
> field that looks like a sample size. Three quantities on this record are called `n` and two of them
> count different things: a task, an episode, a question.

**What the lane can now say it cannot do.** At 68 tasks and complete discordance the floor is
33.98pp; at the last pairing's discordance, 21.41pp; and the whole 115-task retail split reaches only
26.13pp. **No design on this lane resolves a 5pp effect.** R119 states those bounds in its
registration instead of discovering them after the dispatch, which is the difference between a
result and a number.

## 34.149 An instrument whose input is not in the artefact cannot be re-read, and two numbers that disagreed in one file

R119's artefact carries both censuses, two keys apart:

```
fold:  units 631, folded 0, groups 0, atLeastTwo 0, max 1
merge: shapes 53, mergeable 30, support.atLeastTwo 10, atLeastThree 5, max 5
```

**They are the same question asked of one store, and they disagree by everything.** That is a
*verification* defect before it is a mechanism defect: a reader handed this file is handed two
answers to "how much recurrence does this store have", with nothing in the file saying which is about
what. The audit is supposed to be the reader who notices, and it printed both for three rounds without
noticing, because each line was read inside its own paragraph.

Three separate failures, in increasing order of cost.

**First — the artefact did not carry the input.** `storeItems` recorded each item's statement, its
scope, its status and a count of its evidence, and not the routine the fold keys on. So the fold census
was **unfalsifiable from the file that printed it**: a reader could not distinguish

- a store with no two records of one routine, from
- a key with no input.

It was the second, and the only route to that answer was reading the extractor's source. An
instrument whose input is not in the artefact is not an instrument; it is a claim with a number
attached. The repair is one field — `storeItems[].shape`, with `shapeCarried` beside it so a projection
that never asked is distinguishable from a store of unnamed routines, the same discipline `scopeDims`
follows after 34.135.

**Second — a sentence that was right for the wrong reason was allowed to become calibration.** R119
printed:

> "the fold removed nothing, so the two arms are one treatment: this delta is the lane's run-to-run
> noise at n = 40"

Both clauses are true. The inference is sound. And the 7.50pp it produced was about to become the
lane's noise floor — the number every future delta on this lane would be measured against. It was
7.50pp because **the treatment failed to apply**, not because the treatment is inert. A null contrast
built on a mechanism that never fired is a measurement of the mechanism's absence, and calling it
noise is a category error that happens to produce a conservative number. Conservative and wrong is
still wrong, and here it was load-bearing for every comparison that follows.

**Third — the gate asserted a different bar than the registration beside it, and its bar was the
lenient one.** This one is the most expensive because the gate is what a reader trusts:

| | stated where | value | who applied it |
|---|---|---|---|
| the registration's bar | prose in `R119-the-regime-paired.md` | lower bound must clear 0.575 → **p ≥ 0.75** | nobody |
| the gate's bar | `sampleGates`, hardcoded | point ≥ 0.575 + 0.05 = **0.625** | CI |

The interval between them is a 12.5pp band in which a dispatch would have been **green** under a file
that says the claim cannot be made. R119 landed below both, so nothing was manufactured this time —
which is exactly why it went unnoticed. A defect that only fires in the band where a run is mediocre
enough to pass the weak gate and good enough to look like a result is the defect most likely to reach
a SOTA table.

The root cause of the third is structural rather than numeric: `sampleGates` accepted
`published: { meets: boolean }` — **a verdict, not a number**. A function that receives a decision
cannot state the rule it applied, so the `criterion` string it printed (`>= published + 0.05`) was a
decoration that could disagree with the boolean. It now takes the value, the ruler and the count,
computes its own verdict, and prints the half-width it subtracted.

**And a fourth, smaller, in the audit's own tooling.** Wiring `TAU_PREREG_FILE` into the driver made
the L4 gate read a registration — and the repo's `scripts/audit.mjs` immediately failed the build
because the parameter had no workflow that could set it. That check came out of 34.148, one round
earlier, and it fired on the first new parameter written afterwards. Recorded here because it is the
first evidence that a check installed for a class of defect catches the next instance of that class
without anyone remembering to look.

**What the audit now asks of any census.** For each number a run prints: *is its input in the
artefact?* If not, the number is a claim. For each pair of numbers that answer the same question: *do
they agree, and if not, which one is about a different object?* R119 had two and they differed by a
factor of everything, and the file offered no way to tell.

## 34.150 The counter counted the arm, the key counted the retries, and the difference had no evidence

R120 was dispatched to answer one question — does the delivery fold work at all on a distilled store —
and it answered **yes** (58 items removed across 162 packs, `unnamed` 650 → 0). It also produced three
defects in the instruments that were supposed to report the answer, and one finding that changes what
this record may claim.

**First — a counter whose value is a function of the mode is not a measurement of the store.** The
pre-registered claim was `fold.groups` non-empty. `foldByShape` increments that count only when it
folds, and it folds only in `collapse` mode:

```ts
const meetsFloor = members.length > 1 && support >= minSupport;
if (meetsFloor && options.mode === 'collapse') { … groups.push(…) }
else if (members.length > 1 && support < minSupport) { refused += 1; }
```

On `per-failure` the count is therefore **zero whether the store recurs or not** — and `per-failure` is
the arm the field was read from. The registration named a field its own arm could not move. That is not
an unlucky guess; it is a category error in how a registration picks its reading, and it fails in the
direction that looks like rigour: the arm *cannot* succeed, so the census "refutes" the mechanism while
the collapse arm beside it removes 58 items.

The repair counts both populations and names them apart: `groups` (folded), `suppressed` (met the floor,
the unit did not fold it), `refused` (did not meet the floor), `unnamed` (never entered a group).
`groups + suppressed + refused` is now the population of multi-member buckets, and the printed line
states which of them is zero and why. **The rule for any registration that follows: a claim may only
name a field that the arm it runs on can vary.** A field that is constant by construction is not a
conservative claim; it is a claim that cannot be graded.

**Second — the packer refills, so a delivery-side fold is a substitution and the control measured
nothing.** The registration predicted the collapse arm's `items/req` and `chars/req` would fall. They
rose (4.012 → 4.025, 2,187 → 2,189) while 58 items were folded out. `buildPack` folds the *selection*
and `makePack` then renders under a character budget: a line saved is a line spent on the next-ranked
candidate. So the arm did not deliver *less*; it delivered *different*. Its own containment control
reports `0 request(s)`, because after the refill no treatment pack is a subset of its control — the
control was built to verify a removal and the treatment performs a replacement, so the control silently
measured nothing for 162 requests and printed a sentence that reads like a clean check.

The measurement is now possible: `PackCensus.ledger` records the ids each request was served, and
`ledgerDiff` prices the substitution — positions repacked, records in, records out. **A fold whose
placement is the delivery boundary, in a packer that fills to budget, is a re-ranking of what is
delivered and not a reduction of it.** That is a design fact, and it was mis-specified in R109's own
decision table, which described the fold as "the unit the model sees, and nothing else" without saying
that the unit count cannot change.

**Third — the key counted a retry as a step, so every census keyed on a routine has been reporting the
episode's retry pattern.** In R120's store:

| shape | items |
|---|---|
| `return_delivered_order_items` | 5 |
| `cancel_pending_order > cancel_pending_order` | 4 |
| `modify_pending_order_address > modify_user_address > modify_pending_order_items` | 4 |

`44 of 62` sampled shapes carry a consecutive repeat, and one routine is two keys — `cancel_pending_order`
once, `cancel_pending_order > cancel_pending_order` four times. A call repeated because the previous one
failed is the same step tried twice; a key that counts it as two steps gives one routine as many keys as
it has retry patterns. Distinct shapes on the sample fall **31 → 27** under run-length collapse.

This is not a new class of defect, it is the **same** one as the fold key, one level down: the census was
reporting a property of its key and calling it a property of the store. `merge.shapes: 53,
mergeable: 30, support.atLeastTwo: 10` — the numbers R99's merge arm was justified by, and quoted in
ROADMAP as the store's structure — are inflated and deflated by that arithmetic respectively. The repair
collapses a *run* and not the sequence (`calculate > get_product_details > calculate` stays two
calculations around a lookup), which is asserted in both directions so the fix cannot be widened by a
reader who sees only one test.

**Fourth — the artefact carried the store and the score and dropped the packs, so the round's central
difference could not be attributed.** R119 scored 0.600 and R120 0.750 on one lane, one split, one seed,
one model, one `n`. Fifteen points, larger than every effect this record has reported since R85, and
**neither artefact can say which packs differed**: `pack` kept counts, `served.byItem` kept per-item
totals, and the per-request id list was discarded. `queries` had already established the key — position
in the phase — for the *question*; the answer was not recorded at the same granularity, so the
reproduction was one-directional.

The ledger closes it. It is the same discipline as `storeItems[].shape` one round earlier and
`scopeDims` before that: **an instrument that cannot be re-read from its own artefact is a claim, not a
measurement** — and the cost of not having it here was a 15pp difference that the record can describe
and cannot explain.

**What the round establishes.** Three of this record's instruments — the fold key, the fold census, the
merge census — were each reporting their own key. The store is not 53 routines; it is fewer, and it is
fewer than this record can currently count. The next arm's prediction is therefore about a store measured
with the repaired key, and the first thing it must report is that census, not a score.

**And a note on what a single draw can look like.** R119's registration said a 0.60 point spans
[0.448, 0.752] at n = 40. R120 came back at **0.750** — the upper edge of that interval, from a run in
which the mechanism under test folded nothing on the arm being scored. A reader given only the second
number would have called it a 15pp improvement from a key repair that could not have touched the score.
The record's refusal to claim a score at this `n` is not modesty; it is the only reading that survives
being repeated.

## 34.151 The metric was the defect: a 15pp difference produced by one episode

The four defects above are instruments reporting their own key. This one is the **response variable**,
and it is the most consequential because every result in this record is expressed in it.

R119 and R120 ran one lane and scored 0.600 and 0.750. Read at the episode level:

| | R119 | R120 |
|---|---|---|
| episodes passed | 140 / 160 | 141 / 160 |
| rate | 0.8750 ±5.12pp | 0.8812 ±5.01pp |
| tasks at 4/4 · 3/4 · 2/4 · 1/4 · 0/4 | 24 · 13 · 2 · 1 · 0 | 30 · 6 · 1 · 1 · 2 |
| `pass^4` | 0.600 | 0.750 |

**One episode apart over one hundred and sixty, fifteen points apart in the headline.** The reason is
in the estimator's definition: `pass^4` on a task is one exactly when all four trials passed, so it
estimates `p⁴` averaged over **forty tasks**, while `p` is estimated over **one hundred and sixty
episodes**. A run at p ≈ 0.88 that misses twice in the same task loses that task entirely; a run at the
same rate that misses once in each of two tasks keeps both. The two are indistinguishable at 160
episodes and 15pp apart at 40 tasks.

**What this invalidates, stated as narrowly as the evidence allows.** It does not invalidate the
record's arm comparisons against each other — they are all measured the same way, and a randomized
paired comparison is still a comparison. It invalidates **ranking a 40-task `pass^4` against the
competitor's 114-task one**, and it explains why a dozen arms at this `n` produced almost no resolvable
deltas: each was graded on the tail of four trials rather than on the rate.

**The countermeasure is not a different benchmark, it is a second denominator.** Both are reported:
`rate` (episodes, SE 2.6pp) is the measurement; `pass^4` (tasks, SE 7.7pp) is the interface to ALTK's
table and is quoted with its `n`. A headline above `rate⁴` is then a **finding** — the misses clustered
— and R120's 0.750 against a `rate⁴` of 0.6031 is the first instance. `arm-rate.ts` computes all three
from the artefact, and `pnpm eval:pack-repeat` prints them beside the flip table so no future pair of
runs is read at one level only.

**And a rule that follows for every claim this record makes from here.** A metric whose resolution is
coarser than the effect being claimed is not a conservative metric; it is a coin. The half-width at
n = 40 is 15.18pp, the run-to-run difference measured here is 15.00pp, and for two rounds the record
described the second as "the noise floor" while measuring with the first. They were the same number for
the same reason.

## 34.152 A mean cannot see a monopoly, and 100% served means the gate was not applied

Two hundred words into R120's artefact there is a sentence that has been read as a healthy store for eight
rounds: `served 162 of 162 (mean 4.0 items)`. Both halves of it are wrong as readings.

**The mean is over renders, and the question is over records.** R120's `served.byItem` — a field that has
existed since R93 — says one of 63 served records took **88 of the 162 requests (54.3%)**, that the five
most-served took **30.9% of 650 renders**, that **8 records were rendered exactly once**, that **10 of the 73
stored records never reached a prompt at all**, and that `exp(entropy)` over the render distribution is
**38.5** — of 63. A pack described as "four items" is not a store described as "four items"; it is a
distribution whose first member is a monopoly. **The mean is the one summary that cannot see it**, and this
record has published the mean as though it were a health metric.

**And the record is a negative instruction about a rare situation.** The 88-request record's `when` is *"The
question contains a check-only clause for an item alongside a separate item to actually return"*; its
statement says no return action is invoked when the user asks to check but not to process. Most of the 88
requests are not about return-checking. On those the rule can only suppress a call — which is the read-time
generalization arXiv 2611.07554 measures at 35–81% unsafe action with memory against ≈0 without.

**`served 162 of 162` is not coverage; it is the floor's default.** `buildPack` keeps every hit when
`minCoverage <= 0`, `AS_IS_FLOOR` is 0, and a registration that does not name a floor emits 0. The artefact's
own retention curve on the same 650 pairs shows the rungs: 0.05 still serves **162 of 162**, 0.10 serves 154
and empties 8, **0.15 serves 75 and empties 87**, 0.20 serves 36. So the delivery rate has been 100% because
nothing was withheld, and the first rung that withholds anything withholds more than half the traffic.

This is the third time in five rounds that a number has been read as a property of the world when it is a
property of the harness: `fold.groups` (zero by construction on the arm that read it), the pack's `items/req`
(a substitution disguised as a size), and now `served` (a default disguised as a coverage). **The rule that
generalises: before a census field is allowed into a claim, ask what would have to be true for it to be
false. `served = requests` is falsifiable only if some request *could* be refused, and at floor 0 none can.**

**What the record now prints, and why both halves are needed.** `ServedCensus.concentration` —
`topOne`, `topFive`, `once`, `effective` — computed from the same counts `byItem` already holds, so a
readback can recompute it and a reader does not have to. `servedLineOf` puts it on the run's log beside the
pack line, because the pack line is what everyone reads. And `denominatorFieldsOf` puts `episode_rate`, its
interval and `rate_to_the_k` on **every** `poc-l4` line, since the alternative is what R120 did: print
`pass4=0.75` over 141 of 160 episodes and let a reader call the difference an improvement.

**The generalization the record is allowed to draw from four null signals and one concentration.** Content
(which rules enter the pack), persistence (whether advice is stored) and provenance (whether the advice is
about this question) have each been measured null on BIRD; quantity costs **1.7pp per rule injected**; the
delivery fold substitutes rather than reduces; and the pack is served on every request. Those five readings
have one common object: **the decision that was never made is whether to speak at all**. R123 makes it.

## 34.153 The pass keyed on the one string this record had already disqualified

R121 was bought to spend a number the record has quoted since R99: `merge.support.atLeastTwo`, the count of
routines taught by two or more corrections. It ran, considered 79 items, and merged **none**, with all four
refusal counters at zero. Both halves of that sentence are defects.

**First — the pass cannot report the population it did not test.** `consolidateKnowledge` walks every pair and
`continue`s on three conditions before any counter increments:

```ts
if (leftItem.kind !== rightItem.kind) continue;
if (scopeKey(leftItem.scope) !== scopeKey(rightItem.scope)) continue;
const overlap = overlapOf(leftIndex, rightIndex);
if (overlap < threshold) continue;
```

So `groups: 0, merged: 0, refusedCondition: 0, refusedPayload: 0, refusedDuplicateEvidence: 0,
refusedLinkage: 0` is consistent with *the store had nothing to merge* and with *the key removed everything*,
and the record read it as the first. The census now counts `pairs` (`C(n,2)`), `skippedKind`,
`skippedScope` and `skippedOverlap`, and `consolidationLineOf` prints them with a sentence naming the
filter that took the largest share. **A zero that cannot say which zero it is has been this record's most
expensive defect class, and this is its fourth instance.**

**Second — and the reason the answer is the second one.** The store's own sample:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| items | 64 |
| distinct `scopeKey` | **60** |
| buckets with two items | 4 |
| pairs tested | 4 of 2,016 |

`scopeKey` includes `scope.intent`, the field the distiller fills with free text. In R121's store one routine
appears as `cancel pending orders`, `exchange order item`, `update addresses`, `multi-action request`,
`address update`, `exchange items`, `return delivered items` and `multi-action order management`. **R119
established exactly this and wrote it into the key's doc comment**: the intent string cannot key anything
(`return_items` / `return_item` / `items to return` — nine of sixty-four items shared one spelling and every
one of them still carried `supportTasks: 1`). The fold's key was moved off it. The consolidator's linkage key
was not, and the pass ran for the first time two rounds after the string was disqualified.

**Third — the number that justified the arm is a census of routines, not of claims.** The same artefact
carries `merge: { corrections 73, shapes 44, mergeable 41, support { max 8, atLeastTwo 12, atLeastThree 5 } }`
— keyed on `actionShapeOf`, the correction's tool sequence. It says 41 of 44 routines had two or more
corrections. It does not say, and cannot say, that any two of those corrections wrote the **same claim**;
`supportTasks` is 1 on **79 of 79** items. Two mergers, one store, one day, opposite readings, and the
routine-keyed one has been read as a merge opportunity for twenty rounds.

**The rule this round adds.** A census and a mechanism may only be compared when they are keyed on the same
object. `merge.support.atLeastTwo` and `consolidation.merged` were quoted in one sentence of R121's
registration and they count different things: routines taught twice, and claims written twice. The
registration should have asked for the second and cited the first.

**What it would have cost to know.** Zero. The sweep in the same artefact said `threshold 0.40: groups=1
merged=1 crossTask=1` and eight rows of zeros above it, and the store's `scopeKey` distribution is a
`Counter` over a field the artefact carries. Neither was read, because the run printed nine `sweep:` rows and
no operating-point row — the instrument that would have surfaced both was the printer added this round.

## 34.154 The counter that was written, self-tested, and never called

`microglia_agent.py` has exposed `memory_stats()` since **2026-10-24** (`ff6ad8f`, "give the lane something
that can actually run a tau2 split"), 22 days and roughly sixty rounds ago. Its docstring states its purpose
— *"What the run should record about the sidecar, so a zero is explainable"* — and it returns three fields
the lane has quoted ever since:

```python
return {"recall_url": _memory_url(), "recall_failures": _failures, "recalls": _recalls}
```

**No caller existed.** `grep -rn "memory_stats" eval/` returned exactly one non-selfcheck hit: its own
definition. `run_split.py` builds `diagnostics` from `diagnostics_of(simulations)` and `usage_stats()`, and
`usage_stats()` counts the *provider's* tokens and calls. The sidecar's own counters were never added. So
every artefact this lane has written was silent about the one number that decides whether a memory arm
measured a memory at all: how many requests reached the facade, and how many of them the facade answered.

**Why it survived ten audits.** The self-check kept it green. `memory_stats_exposes_the_recall_count` calls
the function, asserts its keys, and passes — which is precisely the failure mode `scripts/check-coupling-ledger.mjs`
was carved out of `ci.yml` to escape: *"An inline script cannot be tested … a predicate that always returned
true would have looked exactly like a passing build."* Here the predicate was a **caller-side** test on a
function nobody called. A green test that exercises a dead entry point certifies the entry point, not the
pipeline, and this record has now paid for that shape four times: R56 (a knob nobody sent), R118 (an
instrument with no input), R121 (`merge.support.atLeastTwo` counting the wrong population), R124 (a key
nobody moved). The fifth form is more embarrassing than the others because the instrumentation was *already
written*, and the missing part was one dictionary key.

**What was added instead, and why the shape matters.** `diagnostics.memory` now carries `recall_url`,
`recalls`, `recall_failures`, `recall_empty` and `silent_because`, written **only for a phase whose agent is
the microglia one**. A phase that ran no sidecar omits the block rather than reporting `recalls: 0`, because
a zero there is the defect this whole audit section is about: it reads as "the memory was never asked"
rather than "no memory was wired". `speakLineOf` then prints the partition

```
recalls = served + withheld (by reason) + failed
```

as arithmetic rather than as prose, so a reader can check it against the artefact's own fields, and it prints
`margin 0 (the default: every non-empty pack is served)` at the default rather than the bare `0` that a
previous round read as a coverage figure.

**The generalisation, in the form this record can act on.** A census field earns its place only when
(a) something writes it, (b) something prints it, and (c) the printed line makes its own denominator visible.
`memory_stats` satisfied none of the three and every local gate was green. The check that would have caught
it is not a test of the function but a test of the **artefact**: for each field the lane claims to record,
assert that a real run's JSON contains it. That check does not exist yet, and it is the cheapest thing on
this roster to add.

## 34.155 A threshold is a quantile, and this record kept naming them without the distribution

`buildPack` has withheld packs on three different grounds across thirteen rounds, and every floor it was
dispatched with was chosen the same way: by intuition, from a handful of remembered numbers.

| floor | what it gates | how the value was chosen |
|---|---|---|
| `minCoverage` | does the rule mention the question | "0.15 sounded strict" |
| `minEvidence` | was the rule observed twice | 2, because two is corroboration — the one floor with an argument |
| `speakMargin` | does the store prefer one answer | **not chosen, and that is the finding** |

The third column is the audit. For the first two, the record has since paid for the intuition: the
retention curve over the 650 committed pairs shows the coverage floor is **not** a curve at all —

```
floor  served  emptied
0.05     162        0
0.10     154        8
0.15      75       87
0.20      36      126
```

— a cliff between two adjacent rungs, so a registration naming 0.10 and one naming 0.15 are not two doses
of one treatment, they are "memory speaks" and "memory is silent" with a number in between pretending to
be a knob. `minEvidence: 2` has the same shape for a different reason: on BIRD, **all 1,296** distilled
rules came from a single correction, so the floor that "requires corroboration" injects nothing and its
measured effect (−2 to −4pp) is arithmetically zero in one corpus and 96.43% retention in the other. One
number, two worlds, and the number is a property of the corpus rather than of the policy.

**The generalisation this record can act on.** A threshold over a scored population is a **quantile of
that population**, and a quantile cannot be chosen before the distribution is observed. Every floor in
this codebase gates on a score whose distribution is a property of the *store* — of the embedder, the
corpus, the pack budget, the distiller's phrasing — and the store is different in every dispatch. Naming
a rung from memory is therefore not "choosing a strict threshold"; it is choosing an unknown dose and
reporting the outcome under the dose's name.

**What R123 did about it.** The mechanism was built and left **unrung**. The margin between the top two
candidates is already computed on every request, so a registered arm at `speakMargin: 0` records the
ladder — seven rungs, each priced in withheld requests exactly — for the price of a control run. R123's
rung is then chosen by a rule fixed in `prereg/R123a-the-margin-census.md` **before** the data exists:
the smallest rung withholding 15-40% of the rivaled population; else the largest, with the ladder as its
evidence; and if the smallest rung already withholds more than 40%, **the arm is not run on that store**,
because a gate that removes two requests in five has replaced the store rather than filtered it.

**The cost of not doing this, measured in this record.** R121 and R122 each cost about a dollar and each
returned a rate whose interval could not separate it from the control — 141 of 160 against 133 of 160,
p = 0.2668 — while the population that would have explained *why* went unrecorded. Two dollars bought two
inconclusive rates and no distribution. One dollar spent on a census first would have priced every
subsequent rung and told the reader, in advance, that the traffic was not separable at the rung they were
about to buy.

## 34.156 The census measured a form that was instructed to fail it

`faithfulness` has printed `0 of 667 entity(ies) kept (0.0%)` on four consecutive dispatches. Three
write-ups treated it as the writer's failure — including 34.150, which used it as the example of a number
"reported every round and never attacked". It was attacked this round by reading the prompt:

```text
- A statement is a rule, not a report of the case that taught it. "Questions that name a race join
  results to races on raceId" is a rule; "the query answering <one question> selects forename, surname
  and driverRef" restates one answer and must not be returned.
```

That is the `lesson` form — the form every τ² arm on this lane has run. `lexicon` forbids "the values of
this case" outright; `procedure` forbids any table, column, alias or literal. **A store written by any of
the three cannot contain the corrections' argument values**, and the census counted exactly that absence
as a loss on the writer's ledger.

**Why the module could not see it.** `faithfulnessOf` was given rows of entities, items, and an optional
predicate — everything a *property of the write* needs, and nothing about what the write was **asked** to
do. The docstring's framing ("what was destroyed at write time") carried the assumption that any absent
entity is a destroyed entity, and a docstring is not a check. The same shape as 34.152: a mean that could
not see a monopoly, a rate that could not see a form.

**The fix is a label, not a number.** The rate is unchanged; `faithfulnessOf` takes the form and reports
`formForbidsTheCase`, and the line prints

```text
faithfulness: 0 of 667 entity(ies) kept (0.0%), ... [the lesson form instructs the distiller not to
restate the case, so this rate measures the form]
```

The set is written out rather than parsed from the prompt: a predicate that read the prompt would silently
change meaning the day the prompt was reworded — the reason `scripts/check-coupling-ledger.mjs` exists as a
file rather than as an inline heredoc in `ci.yml`.

**The generalisation, in a form that can be checked.** A census has three parts, and this record has now
mis-specified each of them at least once: a **population** (34.152's mean over a monopoly), a **denominator**
(34.151's two episode counts), and a **counterfactual** — what the number would have been if the mechanism
had not been there. `faithfulness 0 of 667` had a correct population and a correct denominator and a wrong
counterfactual: the right comparison is not "did the store keep the value" but "would a form that permits
the value have kept it", and the second is only answerable by running one. R122 is that run.

**What it costs to keep finding these.** Six censuses in this record have had a defect of this family, and
five were found by writing the line that prints them rather than by reading the code that computes them.
The instrument that catches the seventh is the one 34.154 named and this round shipped for its own field: a
test that reads the real payload across the boundary and asserts the reader sees it. It would not have
caught *this* one — the payload was correct — which is why the check has to be a question about the
population, asked in the registration, and not a check about the shape of the JSON.

## 34.157 The metric was refuted by arithmetic three times, and the third time it printed the same rate beside two headlines

R124's evaluation carries two numbers from one set of 160 episodes:

```
memory    pass4=0.675 episode_rate=0.8812
reference pass4=0.575 episode_rate=0.8063
```

R120's evaluation carried:

```
memory    pass4=0.750 episode_rate=0.8812
```

**The same rate to four decimal places, seven and a half points apart in the headline.** R119 completes the
set at `0.8750 / 0.6000`. Three dispatches, one lane, one split, one seed, one model, one `n`:

| run | `episode_rate` | `pass^4` | what changed between them |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R119 | 0.8750 | 0.6000 | — |
| R120 | 0.8812 | 0.7500 | the fold's key, which moved 58 items across 162 packs |
| R124 | 0.8812 | 0.6750 | the merge key, which moved 4 items into 3 groups |

The mechanism between R120 and R124 is a **merge of four items**. The headline moved 7.5pp on it. That is
the third independent confirmation of Appendix AN.1 and it removes the last reason to compute the quantity:
`pass^4` is `p⁴` averaged over 40 Bernoulli draws, so its variance is `4p³(1−p)/40` against the rate's
`p(1−p)/160` — at `p = 0.88`, a standard error of **7.7pp against 2.6pp**. A metric whose noise exceeds every
effect this record can buy is not a metric, it is a coin with a memory of the last four throws.

**What the coincidence means for the literature this lane compares against.** ALTK publishes `0.6754` and
`0.675`. The record has spent three rounds asking whether those are two populations or two measurements; the
answer is both, and this round adds the one nobody can supply: **on this lane, `0.675` and `0.750` are the
same measurement.** Any published `pass^k` on a 40-task split carries an interval of ±15pp, so a table that
orders two such entries has ordered two draws.

**The instrument that produced the wrong reading was not the score, it was the census.** Two gates failed:

- `l4-pass4` compares against `published + half-width` = `0.7202`. At `n = 40` the bar is a 14.5pp climb, and
  0.675 does not make it. Correct refusal, useless information.
- `l4-effect-resolved` compares `10.00pp` against a **26.21pp** minimum detectable difference. Correct
  refusal, and the number that names the actual problem: this lane's whole arm budget is below its own
  resolution.

**The defect this run appears to surface is a denominator, and §34.158 corrects this paragraph.** `unnamed`
is **52 of 697 units** where R120 printed **0 of 650**, and the first reading — a merge that costs the pack
its shape — is wrong: the artefact attributes all 52 renders to **three rubric-only items** that have never
carried a shape, and R120's own sample was the same 62-of-64. The field counts renders where the defect is
items, which is why a store that did not change appeared to change the moment its two weakest records entered
a pack.

The four mechanism criteria R124 registered all held (`merged 4`, `crossTaskGroups 3`, `support ≥2 0→2`,
`max 1→3`), and the population prediction missed by 2.7–4.8× (`2,415` pairs against `500–900`). Both facts
belong in the same paragraph: **the merge fired, and the cost of the merge pass was budgeted at a third of
what this store actually produces.** A registration that names a population has to be graded on it, and this
one was wrong in the direction that makes the next dispatch cheaper to size rather than dearer.

## 34.158 Three items, fifty-two renders, and the paragraph this record had to take back

§34.157 inferred a defect and the artefact refuted it in the same hour. The census line was:

```
[tau2] pack: ... fold 0 of 697 units (0 groups, 40 suppressed by the unit, 0 refused, 52 unnamed)
```

against R120's `fold 0 of 650 units (0 groups, 14 refused for want of a second task)` with **no `unnamed`
suffix at all** — and the record printed `unnamed 0` only when the value is zero, so R120 read as proof that
`callsOfStatement` had been repaired. Between the two runs the only change on this path is the merge, and 52
is not 4. The inference wrote itself: *a merge that costs the pack its shape*.

**It is wrong, and the arithmetic that refutes it is three lines long.** `pack.ledger` carries 161 packs and
their ids; `storeItems.items` carries a 64-item sample with a `shape` on each. Joining them:

| id | renders | shape | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `k_01hf7uaq7f_5pqmn` | 8 | **none** | `procedure`, `reasonCode: user_intent_update`, `supportTasks: 1` |
| `k_01hf7uaq7e_6w2am` | 17 | **none** | `constraint`, `reasonCode: completeness`, `supportTasks: 1` |
| `k_01hf7uaq6t_5whbr` | 27 | not in the sample | the third of them, inside the 6 omitted items |

`8 + 17 + 27 = 52`. Every unnamed render is one of **three items**, none of them merged (`supportTasks: 1`,
`evidence: 1`), and none of them new: **R120's own artefact reports `shapeCarried: true` with `shape` on 62
of 64 sampled items** — the same two-of-64 gap §PROGRESS 200 recorded as a success.

**The mechanism is not the merge and it is older than the census that showed it.** `shapeByTaskOf` skips a
correction whose `actions` are empty, with a stated reason: *"a correction that called nothing taught no
routine, so it has no entry."* A rubric-only correction is exactly that — retail states no call on seven of
its 114 tasks — and the claim the rubric wrote is a sentence with no `A:` line, so the fold's extractor has
nothing to read and the fallback has no entry to find. The item is unnamed by construction, and it has been
since R120. What changed is that these three records **entered a pack**: with the store consolidated from 70
to 66, their relative rank cleared the budget, and 52 renders followed.

So the field measures **renders** while the defect is **three items**. That is the eighth time in this
record that a counter's denominator decided the reading, and the first time the denominator was right about
the traffic and wrong about the population — `52` is a true statement about 697 units and a misleading one
about a store. A census that says `3 item(s) / 52 render(s)` cannot be read either way, and adding the item
count is free.

**What is left, after the correction.** Two things, and only one of them is a treatment:

1. **The counter.** Print both denominators. No artefact changes, no run changes, and the next reader cannot
   make the inference this paragraph had to take back.
2. **The three records have no key.** A `procedure` carrying `user_intent_update` and a `constraint`
   carrying `completeness` are not noise — they are the two polarities the store is *about*, and the fold
   cannot group either of them with its siblings because there are no siblings: a rubric-only correction
   teaches one task, so its item has support 1 and no routine. Whether to give them a key is a real question
   — `rubric:<reasonCode>` would fold the two `completeness` records of a store, which is a merge on the
   host's vocabulary rather than on the corpus's — and it is registered rather than assumed.

**The rule this adds.** An inference of the form "X changed and the census moved" needs the census's
denominator joined to the population it claims to describe. §34.157 had the merge, had the number, and had
the direction; what it did not have was the join, and the join took one artefact and forty lines of Python.
The cost of the check is the reason it belongs in the readback and not in the dispatch.

## 34.159 A refutation clause fired on a wire that was not connected, and a null result was the most expensive thing this record could have believed

R123a's registration contained one refutation and it was the right one: *if `rivaled` is zero, no rung has a
population to act on and the margin gate is dead on this store*. The run printed `0 rivaled request(s)` over
164 requests, and the sentence was true of the payload and false of the store.

```
served.meanPerRequest   4.05
served.distinct         61 of 76 items
pack.summary.meanIds    4.05
memory.rivaled          0
```

The last row is arithmetically impossible next to the first three, and that impossibility is the whole audit.
`startRecallFacade` answered `{ rendered }` — a response with one field — because the design note that put the
census in-process was written when the only reader was the driver's own `packReadings`. R123a is the first
registration that reads a margin ladder, and it reads it from Python, across a socket. `_margins` never
received a value; `len([])` printed as `0`.

**Why this class is worse than a crash.** A crash ends a dispatch and costs a dollar. A zero that looks like a
measurement ends a *question*: the record would have written "the margin gate has no population on a distilled
τ² store", retired R123, and moved on — with the real answer, whatever it is, unmeasured. The three prior
instances in this record (§34.154's counter with no caller, §34.155's threshold mistaken for a curve, §34.158's
census counting renders) each cost a round. This one would have cost a mechanism, and the only reason it did
not is that the artefact carried three other numbers that disagreed with it.

**The rule that comes out of it is arithmetic, not discipline.** A census whose value is zero must be
accompanied, in the same artefact, by a second count of the same quantity that cannot be zero for the same
reason. Here that is `meanPerRequest`: an empty ranking and a four-item pack cannot both be true, and no amount
of care in reading would have caught it as reliably as the contradiction did. So the repair is not "be
careful with zeros" — it is:

1. **the wire carries the field** (`decision`, only when the pack has one, so no other host's bytes move);
2. **the reader counts its own arrivals** (`_census`), and reports `rivaled: null` — a distinct value from `0`
   — when nothing arrived;
3. **the measurer counts the same quantity again** (`PackCensus.margins`), so the two halves of one run can be
   compared without a third party;
4. **the contract test crosses the boundary with real bytes** (`--parse-decision` over a live response),
   because the previous contract test handed the Python half a fixture it had written itself.

**Two predictions that were graded and one that was not.** `merged`, `crossTaskGroups`, `support ≥2` and
`maxSupport` all held in R124. R123a's population prediction did not fire because it was never measured. Both
facts are recorded here rather than in a footnote, because a record that only reports the criteria it could
check is a record that cannot tell an untested criterion from a passed one.

## 34.160 The ladder a decision rule selects on existed only in a job log, and the block it lived in was dropped by the projection

R123a's decision rule is arithmetic and was fixed before the data: *the rung is the smallest one whose withheld
share is at least 15%, provided it is at most 40%*. Grading it requires one number per rung. The run produced
them, and the artefact did not have them:

```
$ grep -c margin_ladder eval/results/arms/memory/poc-l4.json
0
$ grep -o 'ladder [0-9. /]*' job.log
ladder 0.01 13 / 0.02 22 / 0.05 49 / 0.10 82 / 0.15 105 / 0.20 118 / 0.30 145
```

**A reading that survives only in a log cannot be re-examined.** The log is retained for ninety days; the
artefact is the record. Every other census in this lane ships in the artefact, and this one shipped as a
formatted sentence in a 103 KB text file that had to be downloaded and grepped — by hand, once, with no way for
a later round to recompute it from the arm, and no contract test that could have failed when the field was
renamed.

**Two independent causes, and the second is the one that matters.**

1. **The ladder was computed on the far side of the socket.** `margin_ladder`, `margin_p10/p50/p90` live in
   `memory_stats()`, which runs in the agent process; the artefact is assembled in the driver's TypeScript
   half from `packReadings`. That design was deliberate for R127 — the Python half *prices* the rung, and the
   TypeScript half counts the same population so the two can be compared — but pricing and *recording* are
   different jobs, and only the first was assigned.
2. **The driver read `diagnostics.memory` and dropped it.** `speakLineOf(SPEAK_MARGIN, primary.diagnostics?.memory)`
   is the only consumer of that block in the whole driver. `margin_ladder`, `census`, `rivaled`,
   `recall_url` and `episodeStarts` were computed, printed into a line, and thrown away: **no arm artefact in
   this record has ever carried a `tau2.memory`**.

Cause 2 has a consequence that was not visible until it was written down: **R128's instrument could not have
fired on any run.** `pairAttribution` reads `memory.tau2?.memory?.episodeStarts`, and the projection that would
have written it did not exist. The registration said the readback was `$0` on the next artefact; the field it
joins on had no writer. That is §34.154's shape — a counter with no caller — one layer out: a *reader* with no
writer, with a green gate on both ends.

**The repairs are three, and each is the same rule at a different level.**

- **The ladder is counted where the decisions are.** `marginCensus` runs in `packCensus`, over the same
  `decision.margin` values the pack already carries, so the artefact prices all seven rungs without the wire.
  `MARGIN_RUNGS` is one constant, and a contract test pins the seven values equal to the Python half's list —
  two lists that drift would print two ladders in one artefact rather than failing.
- **The block is projected.** `tau2.memory` is now written from `diagnostics.memory` when the phase has one,
  absent rather than `null` when it does not, which is also what unblocks R128.
- **The line prints the ladder.** The pack line carried `N rivaled of M censused` and now carries
  `p50` and the seven rungs, so a log and an artefact say the same thing and the reader of either can choose a
  rung. The two are compared by construction in the same test that pins the rung list.

**What this audit does not claim.** The rung 0.05 was chosen from the log's numbers, which are the same numbers
`marginCensus` would now produce from the decisions — the two agree because they sort and count the same
population. That agreement is *asserted by construction*, not by having run both on this artefact: the run
predates the repair. The next dispatch is the first that can be read both ways, and the registration names it.

**The general form.** Every reading this record ships must be recomputable from an artefact alone. A number that
exists only in a log, only in a chat, or only in a person's memory of a run is a number the record cannot audit —
and the three prior instances of this class (§34.154, §34.155, §34.158) each cost a round, while this one would
have cost a decision rule its evidence.

## 34.161 Four readers, four ways of saying nothing: how R123's registered mechanism check vanished between a green gate and an artefact

R123 registered one falsifiable core: *the withheld trials score like the reference arm, and worse than the
served ones*. Grading it needs one number — the serve split — computed from three fields the phase already
writes. The phase computed it, printed neither, and the artefact carried neither. Four independent failures had
to line up for that to happen, and each one is a different way for an instrument to be silent.

### 1. The projection table's exhaustiveness had a hole exactly where fields are added

`PROJECTION` is typed `{ readonly [K in keyof Tau2Raw]-?: 'carried' | 'reduced' }`, and its own comment claims
the property this round disproved:

> **a field added to the driver's record fails to compile until it is given a decision.**

A field added as a plain property does. A field added through a spread does not: TypeScript performs
excess-property checking on fresh object literals only, and `...(cond ? {} : { memory })` is a spread member.
Every conditional field in this driver is written that way, which is all of them. So the driver's record grew
two fields, `Tau2Raw` never declared them, the table never ruled on them, and the projection dropped both
without a diagnostic:

```
$ grep -c '"memory"' eval/results/arms/memory/poc-l4.json
0
$ grep -c 'speak: margin 0.05' job.log
1
```

**The check the record trusted was structurally unable to fire.** Its repair is not another comment: the arm
record now names every key the driver emitted that the table has no decision for (`unprojected`), the driver
announces them on stderr, and `l4-projection-complete` fails the pair that carries one. A future spread-added
field is now a red job rather than a silent omission.

### 2. A field named `episodeStarts` recorded positions

The writer appended `_recalls` on every recall, and a recall happens once per episode *and* again when an
episode retries a turn. So the list was one entry per request:

```
R123:  episodeStarts = [0, 1, 2, ..., 161]   over 160 episodes and 162 requests
```

Strictly increasing, one per request, and carrying no boundary at all. The artefact's own comment claimed
"`len(episodeStarts)` is the episode count", which is true only when every episode recalls exactly once — the
assumption the field existed to remove.

The repair records a boundary only when a **fresh instance** opens: τ² constructs one agent per task and trial
(`build_orchestrator` inside `run_single_task`, once per unit — verified in `tau2/runner/batch.py`), so the
instance *is* the episode. A recall inside an episode is counted as `recallRepeats`, and the identity
`len(episodeStarts) + recallRepeats == recalls` is what makes the boundary checkable rather than asserted.

### 3. The join accepted a length check in place of a boundary check

`serveSplit` refused when `episodeStarts.length !== memoryTrials.length`. On R123's data that guard passed —
162 boundaries against 162 trials? No: 162 against 160, so it refused, and the caller printed nothing. Two
layers of silence, and the *passing* case would have been worse: the guard compares lengths, so a boundary that
is one-per-request would be accepted as soon as the trial count matched.

The repair validates the **values**: strictly increasing, inside the ledger, one entry per trial, and each
absence reports which of the three it was with the numbers that disagreed. A boundary is a partition, and a
partition is not a length.

### 4. The caller discarded the sentence that said so

`serveSplitLine` had always been able to say "this arm has no episode boundary". The caller wrote
`if (split !== undefined) print(...)`, so the function's own abstention was unreachable in the one dispatch
that needed it. Same for the turn census, whose absence printed nothing on either arm.

**This is the round's general finding, and it is not about the serve split.** The record has paid nine times for
"a missing field is not a measured zero". The tenth form is one layer out: *a missing field is not printed at
all*, and a reader of a log cannot tell an instrument that abstained from one that was never run. Every
abstention in this lane now names itself — in the log, and in the artefact under `serveSplitAbsent` — and the
pair's gates read the field's presence rather than its value.

### 5. The control arm had no instrument, so half of every pair was missing

`run()` returns early on the reference path, before `observed` is assigned. So **no control artefact has ever
carried a `tau2` block**: no `usage`, no `cost`, no `turnCensus`, no `scenario`. Two consequences had been
attributed to other causes:

- `cache first (unstated): unmeasured` on every pair since R49 — reported each round as a property of the
  provider's accounting, and it is a property of a missing writer.
- R125's paired turn census could never fire. Its registration says the reading rides on the next artefact; the
  control half of the difference did not exist. §34.154's shape again — an instrument with a caller and no
  data — one arm out instead of one field out.

The control arm now builds its record from its phase's own summary line: turns, failures, usage, bill
(divided by the phase's simulation count, not by the provider's per-call view) and the turn census. Its
`train` is empty because it learned nothing, and its `learning` block is zeros because no learning phase ran —
both recorded as absences rather than filled.

**What this audit does not claim.** R123's serve split is not recoverable: the boundary it needed was never
written, and a positional guess would be the defect this section is about. The reading is *unmeasured*, the
registration's refutation condition ("the serve split is level within its intervals") was never tested, and the
arm's directional result — harm share 56.7% against 29.6% ungated — is a sample comparison across two runs, not
a within-arm one.

## 34.162 A phase that can refuse must not take a paid measurement with it

R132 was recorded as blocked on a hundred-line closure, and that was wrong by one layer. The claim was: *the eval
phase's facade callback is also its collector, so a second phase's requests would enter `pack.ledger`,
`servedPackSizes` and `useObservations`*. Two of those three are **per call** — `evaluateFacade` declares its
arrays inside its own body, so a second invocation has its own — and the third does not exist. What would
actually have gone wrong is elsewhere, and the difference matters because it decides whether the next reader
believes a blocker:

| the written blocker | the actual hazard it was standing in front of |
| --- | --- |
| "the callback is also its collector" | `scoredArm` writes **module-level** `observedTrials` and `observedUnscored`, so reading the replay's document through it would have overwritten the graded arm's rows |
| "a second facade" | `host.close()` sits in the `finally` immediately after the evals, so a phase added *after* the `try` would have recalled from a closed store |
| "`pack.ledger`" | no such collector: the pack census is a reduction of the per-call readings |

So the repair was two lines of placement, not a refactor. The replay reads its rewards through `bestRewards`,
which takes a document and returns a map, and the phase runs inside the same `try` the evals run in, after the
graded facade so the treatment is known and before the close so the store can still be asked.

**Why write this down.** A blocker recorded at the wrong layer is worse than one recorded vaguely: it sounds
precise, it prices a refactor that is not needed, and it survives the round because nobody re-derives it. The
check that would have caught it is the one this record already applies to artefacts — *name the object* — and it
was not applied to a plan.

**The three absences this round adds.** A rehearsal phase has one more absence than most instruments, because it
is bought rather than carried:

| state | what the artefact carries | what a reader may conclude |
| --- | --- | --- |
| not bought | no `rehearsal` block | the registration never asked; every arm before R132 |
| bought, ran, nothing paired | the block, `reading` absent, `served` measured | the phase answered and the two reward sets share no task |
| bought, refused at the window | the block, `refused: peak-window`, `requests: 0` | no call was made; the store was not asked |

The middle and the last would collapse into one field if `refused` were folded into `requests: 0`, which is why
they are separate: `0 of 0 served` would say the store served nothing, and the one thing a record must not say
about a phase that made no request is that its store had nothing to offer.

**And the sizing refusal is the same principle applied before the spend.** A rehearsal arm carries
`trials x testTasks + 2 x trainTasks` episodes; at R123a's configuration that is 308 episodes and 271 minutes
against a 240-minute job, so the header is refused at read time with the sum in the message rather than
discovered as a cancelled run whose learning half was already paid for. The ceiling is measured (0.75 minutes an
episode plus about 40 for the store) and stays a constant of the reader, not of the dispatch.

**Postscript, same day.** The first dispatch of R132 died before its first episode on
`TAU_REHEARSAL ... received 'true'`: the header bridge prints a boolean as `true`/`false`, and the resolver had
been written and tested against `1`/`0`. Two spellings, two bridges, and a test that asserted the behaviour of the
spelling its author had in mind. It is the same defect as 34.159 one layer up — not a field with no writer, but a
**switch with two writers and a reader that only knew one of them** — and the guard is now that the test feeds the
producer's output (`String(true)`) through the consumer instead of a literal. A reviewer cannot check that
assignment by reading either side alone, which is why it belongs in a test rather than in a convention.

## 34.163 Three dispatches of one arm, and the end of the single-point ranking

§212 promoted the harm share to "the one quantity on this lane that is comparable across backbones" on the
strength of two runs agreeing to 1.6pp. R131 is a third run of that configuration — same store shape, same
split, same headers, same gate setting — and it reads **55.17%**. The three points:

| run | repaired / broke | harm share | 95% | `pass^4` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R123a | 19 / 8 | 29.63% | [15.9, 48.5] | 0.7750 |
| R124 | 22 / 10 | 31.25% | [18.0, 48.6] | 0.7500 |
| **R131** | 13 / 16 | **55.17%** | [37.6, 71.6] | **0.6250** |

**Why the third run is the important one.** Two agreeing runs can always be one configuration measured twice
and one sample that happened to be tight; a third run of the same configuration is the only thing that
distinguishes "stable" from "two draws that landed near each other". It landed 25pp away, in the direction of
the *gated* arm, which means the 27pp gap §213 attributed to the gate is inside the between-dispatch spread of
the ungated arm itself. The gate story is not refuted — its instrument (the ladder, the serve split) still
reads — but it can no longer be supported by this quantity.

**The variance is not a mystery, and it was measurable before the run.** At n ≈ 29 changed trials the harm
share's 95% half-width is ±17pp; the three intervals above overlap pairwise. The record knew the formula — it
printed those intervals itself in §213 — and still read a 27pp difference across two of them as a direction. The
rule that follows is not "be more careful": it is that **a difference smaller than the printed half-width is not
a reading**, and every table in this record that orders two arms must carry the half-width in the row.

**What replaces the ranking, for `pass^4`.** The pair artefact already computes it:

| quantity | value at n = 40 | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resolution.halfWidthPp` | **16.97pp** | the interval around a measured delta |
| `resolution.tasksForFivePp` | **461** | the tasks a 5pp claim needs at this variance |
| `ceiling.tasks` | **114** | every task τ²-retail has |
| `ceiling.halfWidthPp` | **10.05pp** | the best this benchmark can ever do |
| `ceiling.mde80Pp` | **14.37pp** | the smallest effect it can detect at 80% power |

So τ²-retail **cannot** resolve a 5pp difference even if every task in it were run. Any statement of the form
"microglia 0.775 beats ALTK-Evolve 0.675" is therefore a statement about two samples, not about two systems —
and this record has now watched one of those numbers move 15pp under its own feet. The competitive board is
rewritten accordingly in Appendix AU: the column that survives is the *instrument*, not the score.

**What survives, and is worth more than the ranking did.** The serve split reproduced the arm's `episode_rate`
to the last digit (134 of 160 = 83.75% against 0.8375) on a run with no gate; the ladder priced the 0.05 rung at
60 of 160; the attribution table named six items with a negative net over 18–19 episodes each. Those are
readings that a sample of 40 tasks can support, because they are not estimates of a mean — they are censuses of
what the run did.

## 34.164 A denominator that is also the selector

R132 replayed the 74 learnt tasks against the store and read **5 repaired / 9 inert** of the 14 that had failed
without memory. The `inert` cell is defined as "failed without memory, then failed again with it" — and the
without-side is the very draw that **selected** which cases the store was written from. A task that fails two
thirds of the time produces that cell whether or not the store exists, so the cell is a tautology dressed as a
finding.

This is the fourth instance of one family in this record, and the family is worth naming because each instance
looked reasonable on its own:

| instance | the shared denominator | what it laundered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R48 | two arms' readings from **different dispatches** | a treatment effect made of two samples |
| R92 | `pass4` over **29 of 40** tasks with `unscored_tasks: 0` | a score over a population the scorer had shrunk |
| R123 | seven counters that were all **zero** | "nothing happened" for "nothing measured" |
| **R132** | the learn draw as the **baseline** for the replay | task difficulty as a store effect |
| R133 (refusal) | `learnOnly` + `rehearsal` | — and here the *reason* was wrong, not the reading |

**The repair is a second draw, not a smaller claim.** R133 runs the same 74 tasks with the store off and the
same one trial, so `repaired` and `broke` become discordant pairs between two phases that differ only in the
store. The cost is a third pass (~74 episodes, ~$0.13) and the payoff is that `net = repaired − broke` has a
baseline that is not the selector. The control deliberately carries **no** `requests` and **no** `served`: it
has no facade, and `0 of 0 served` would read as a store that found nothing — the misreading 34.162 forbids one
field over.

**And the fifth row is the quieter lesson.** The refusal that stopped `learnOnly` arms from buying a rehearsal
gave a reason that was simply false — "a replay would have nothing to pair against" — when the replay pairs
against the learn half's rewards, which a learn-only arm runs. Nobody would have caught it by reading the
refusal; it was caught by wiring the control and asking what the pairing actually reads. **A wrong reason in a
validation is worse than a missing validation**, because it prices a fix that does not exist and survives every
review that only checks the refusal fires.

## 34.165 Two spreads, one arbiter: I² says which of this record's numbers was ever an estimate

For four rounds this record has had two quantities that moved between dispatches and no way to say whether the
movement was the world or the sample. The pool (§PROGRESS 216) answers it with I² — the share of a spread that
lives *between* dispatches rather than inside them — and the answer sorted the two quantities into opposite
categories:

| quantity | I² | what the movement was | still usable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pass^4` at 40 tasks | **16%** | sampling error the interval already described | **as an estimate with ±19pp**, never as a point |
| harm share at ~29 changed trials | **60%** | the dispatches genuinely disagree | **no** — not until the moderator is found |
| episode rate at 160 | **0%** | nothing: the arms agree within their own error | **yes**, ±4.0pp |

**The uncomfortable half is the middle row.** For two rounds §212/§213 promoted the harm share to the record's one
cross-backbone comparator on the strength of two dispatches agreeing to 1.6pp. A third dispatch 25pp away could be
dismissed as noise if I² were near zero; it is 60%, which means the three numbers are drawn from distributions
with genuinely different means. The record does not know what varies between them — candidates are the store's
composition (83 items, but which ones), the retry control's own sampling, and drift in the model's behaviour — and
until it does, *any* statement of the form "our harm share is X, the literature's is 52%" is a statement about one
dispatch. Appendix AU removes that column for this reason.

**The comfortable half is worth more than it looks.** The episode rate over two arms of one dispatch comes back
with I² = 0 and ±3.96pp. That is the first interval in this record narrow enough for a 5pp claim, and it is not a
new instrument — it is the by-product every arm already prints. A board that ranks on episodes rather than on
`pass^k` is therefore both cheaper and more honest, which is a rare combination.

**The practice rule that follows.** No quantity is quoted from fewer than two dispatches, and nothing is compared
across arms until its I² is under 50%. Both halves are mechanical, and both would have caught the retracted
ranking: AR compared 0.775 with 0.675 from one dispatch each, and §213 read a 27pp harm-share difference across two
intervals that each spanned more than half of it.

**And a line on the module's own honesty.** It prints whether the interval "can order two arms N pp apart" rather
than leaving that to the reader, because the retracted ranking was produced by a reader doing that arithmetic
silently and getting it wrong. A reading that states its own resolution cannot be quoted out of context — and if it
is, the quote carries the refutation with it.

## 34.166 A store is priced per episode, and the pack is what prices it

R133 bought three phases: the held-out half (40 episodes), a replay of the learn half with the store (74), and
the same 74 with the store off. Same backbone, same tasks, same two hours. The artefact carries a bill for each,
and this is the first time the lane has compared them:

| phase | episodes | cost | per episode | prompt tokens | uncached | cache hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| held-out, store on | 40 | $0.2461 | $0.0062 | — | — | — |
| replay, store on | 74 | $0.4847 | **$0.00655** | 8,558,308 | 2,508,270 | **0.7069** |
| control, store off | 74 | $0.1996 | **$0.00270** | 6,068,231 | 594,961 | **0.9020** |

**The store costs 2.43× per episode on identical work**, and the mechanism is not the items' length. A four-item
pack is *different text on every request*, so the provider's prefix cache is replaced rather than reused: 2.5M
tokens arrive uncached against the control's 0.59M, and the hit rate falls eleven points. The three numbers are
one fact — count, cache, bill — and the lane had never printed them side by side because it never ran the same
episodes twice.

**The defect this replaces.** R133's registration priced the arm from R132's "$0.00196 an episode over 262
episodes". R132's own mixture was 228 episodes across two arms at two trials, and the number was carried into a
registration for a *different* mixture: the dispatch cost **$0.9304**, 1.82× the estimated $0.51. A per-episode
price extrapolated from another arm's mixture is a prediction, not a measurement, and this lane has now paid
twice for the distinction (R85's clipped records were the first).

**The rule.** Any arm whose pack differs from its predecessor's must print its own bill beside the control's, in
the same artefact, as cost **per episode** — because the number that matters is not what an arm cost but what an
*episode* costs, and an episode is the only unit both phases have in common. And a registration may quote a
per-episode price only from an arm that ran the same phases; otherwise the estimate carries its own error bar
and the dispatch is held to the upper one, which is what R134's cost section does ($0.55 with the fall priced
in, $0.73 if it does not).

## 34.167 A band whose justification is measured is a band that can be refuted
