**One methodological note worth keeping.** The lane spent four dispatches comparing blocks to controls whose own
readings moved by more than the effects being measured, and found its largest, cleanest contrast the first time two
blocks were compared to each other. The instrument for that (`--relabel`, path-keyed, with the ambiguous-basename
refusal) was written for a hypothetical and fired on its author's first real command; the reading it produced is the
only one in this record whose interval is not dominated by an arm that carries no pack at all.

## 34.243 — Engagement is not an admission test, and the arm that carried nothing reported a gate's effect

**The claim this replaces.** That a treatment arm which diverges from its control on 88% of games has been read by
the model. It has not: an empty prompt is also a different prompt. Run `44841993038` diverged on 121 of 134 games,
produced a computable paired delta, six by-kind rows and a bill, and carried **zero entries in every one of the 134
games**. Every counter in the report was healthy and none of them was about the pack.

**Why the counters could not see it.** `divergence_rate` measures whether the trajectory changed; `help_share` and
`harm_share` divide by the games that changed; `by_kind` splits a delta that exists either way. The pack enters the
artefact only as `pack_entries`, which was recorded per episode and never aggregated — a field that was being
written and never read, which is the same failure as a field that is never written, one layer later.

**What was changed.** `aggregate.py` gains `carried()` and `empty_pack_reason()`. The distribution of
`pack_entries` is printed **above the delta**, and the join refuses two shapes: a pack arm (family `always-in`,
`sham` or `retrieved`, taken from the label before the `@`) whose pack was empty in every game, and a `none` arm
that carried anything. An artefact written before the field existed has no counts and is passed over rather than
failed — the check says what it can see instead of assuming the rest.

**What this class of defect costs, measured.** The void arm's −6.72 pp [−14.93, +1.49] would have been filed as
"the gate is harmful at 0.2", and a second reading — gated 81 against the archived ungated 99, a cross-dispatch
paired delta of −13.43 pp [−22.39, −4.48], p 0.0044 — would have been filed as "the gate costs thirteen points and
the direction of the repair is wrong". Both are numbers a programme can be steered by, and both are the control's
own noise: six `none` readings on these 134 games span 80 to 91.

**The general form.** A voiding condition that is computed from the *outcome* (engagement, divergence) cannot
replace one computed from the *manipulation* (what the prompt contained). The lane had three conditions and all
three were outcome-shaped; the fourth — was the treatment in the prompt — is the only one that could have caught
this, and it costs one counter.

## 34.244 — The gate's premise is false on this corpus: an observation names the room, and the failure is in the action

**The registered hypothesis.** `arXiv:2610.07311`'s repair, ported as a floor on the share of the observation's own
content words a rule must account for. The prediction was that the floor would fire on the games whose observation
names the failing step and stay silent on the rest, making a broad bank behave like a narrow pack.

**The measurement, which needed no dispatch.** A real first observation carries 22 content words after stopwords:
`cabinet`, `countertop`, `garbagecan`, `handtowelholder`, `sinkbasin`, `toilet`, `toiletpaperhanger`, `towelholder`,
`room`, `middle`, `looking`, `quickly`, `see`, plus the task line's `put`, `some`, `spraybottle`, `toilet`, `task`.
Every one of the room's nouns is furniture. The four registered rules are about operations — `inventory`, `put`,
`move`, `receptacle`, `take`. The largest overlap available is **one word**, and one of the three matches is `task`,
which the prompt itself supplies. The floor of 0.2 needs **4.4** words. There is no threshold between 0 and 1 that
would have worked either: the signal is absent, not weak.

**Why the unit tests did not see it.** `test_agent.py`'s gate fixtures use a four-word observation, where 0.2 is a
single shared word and the floor is reachable by construction. The fixture was written to demonstrate the
arithmetic, and it demonstrated it. A threshold whose reachability depends on the length of the text it is measured
against can only be tested against the corpus's own text, and `GateTest` now carries that observation verbatim.

**What replaces it.** `--gate-kind`: select entries by the task the game names, which `task_kind_of` reads from the
gamefile's directory before the first call. It is not a proxy for overlap; it is the operand the overlap was
standing in for. A bank that tags its entries (`"kinds": ["put", "puttwo"]`) is filtered to the game's kind, an
untagged entry is carried everywhere, and a kinds list that does not line up with the rules is refused rather than
zipped — because the misalignment a cap produces (`rules[:cap]` beside an uncut `kinds`) would carry the sentence
the arm believes it dropped.

**What is not claimed.** That a task-kind gate generalises past corpora where the task is a directory name. It is
the harness's own label, and on a corpus whose tasks are not enumerated it does not exist. What generalises is the
sentence: **a memory is selected by what the agent is doing, and a room is not that.**

## 34.245 — One sentence at 489 characters is the best arm in the lane, and a per-sentence price cannot explain it

**The reading.** 112/134 (83.58%) against a control of 88, +17.91 pp [+8.96, +26.87], p < 0.001 — three wins above
the two-sentence pair (109) and thirteen above the four-rule block (99), at 37% of the block's rendered length.

**What it does to the per-sentence slope of AUDIT 34.242.** The slope was −3.4 to −3.7 pp per sentence, measured
between blocks that differed in *which* sentences they carried. R174.1 adds a point at one sentence and the ladder
becomes 112 (1) ≥ 109 (2) > 100 (2, padded) ≈ 99 (4). Two readings follow and they are not the same claim:

1. **A second sentence about the same failing step is worth nothing measurable.** 112 against 109 is three wins,
   inside an interval thirteen wins wide. The product sentence is therefore "one sentence per failing step", not
   "as few sentences as possible".
2. **The slope was never about counting.** The pair and the block differ by two sentences *and* by whether the
   sentences name the failing operation: entries 1–2 are about a desklamp and about search order, entries 3–4 are
   about the two operations most games fail at. 112 − 99 = 13 wins over three extra sentences, of which the two
   task-relevant ones were carried in both arms.

**The claim that is now retired.** "Each sentence costs 3.4 pp of attention" was written as a mechanism and is not
one: it fitted a line through three points whose content differed. What survives is weaker and safer — **a pack
pays for its length and is worth its specificity** — and the next measurement (R175 row 2) is the one that could
restore or refute a count: six sentences, all task-relevant and one per kind, with and without selection.

**One thing this reading changed without being asked to.** The compressed-pair arm built for the format question
(`banks/bank-putpair-terse-2.json`, 508 characters, same two operations) was registered and not bought: a 3–4 pp
effect is below this instrument's 12–14 pp minimum detectable effect, and buying an arm whose answer cannot be
resolved is how a programme spends ¥3.2 on a tie it will then argue about.

## 34.246 — A flag the control cannot obey took four shards, and the control is the whole point of a sweep

**What happened.** R175 row 1 was dispatched as a two-arm sweep, `["none","always-in"]`, with `--gate-kind`. The
treatment arm ran, four of four slices, 69/134. **The control arm failed on all four slices at its first line:**

> `FAIL --gate-kind selects among rules, so it needs an arm that carries one`

The cause is structural rather than clerical. The arm step in `alfworld.yml` writes **one** command line for all
twelve jobs and appends `--rules` only inside `if [ "${ARM}" != "none" ]` — because the control is defined by not
carrying a bank. The gate flag was added outside that branch, so every control job was started with a flag that
selects among a bank it does not have, and the driver's guard — written to stop a treatment paying for a gate with
nothing to gate on — fired on the arm the flag was never meant for.

**Why the driver is where the defect lived.** The guard was correct about treatments and wrong about the process
that starts them. `agent.py` reads one arm; the workflow reads a matrix. A flag whose legality depends on the arm
cannot be an error at the arm level when the arm is one cell of a matrix that the same flag is sent to. The fix is
three lines and the reasoning matters more than the code:

* `--gate-kind` on the control is **inert, not refused**: the control carries no bank, there is nothing to select,
  and its artefact records `gate_kind: null` — which is a true statement about what ran, where a refusal is a
  statement about the dispatch that killed a job that would have been correct.
* `arm_label` keeps the control's name as `none`. `gate_kind` is a knob, and a knob that selects from an empty set
  has not been moved; `none@kind` would have been a second control family, and the one arm every reading in this
  lane is compared against would have stopped being recognisable in `aggregate.py`.
* the dispatcher stops refusing the flag on `--arm none` as well. It was refused there for the same reason and with
  the same effect — and it is a real purchase: re-buying the control of a gated sweep against the same commit is
  the only repair available once such a sweep has been bought without one.

**The rule that now holds it.** `test_cli.py` reads the YAML as text and asserts that every `args+=(--gate…)` line
appears **above** the `ARM != none` branch, that there are two of them, and that the driver's guard is still
written as `arguments.arm != "none" and not any(rule_kinds)`. A structural rule rather than a behavioural one,
because the failure mode is a *tidier-looking* YAML: the flag beside `--rules` reads better, and reads better is
how it was written.

**What it cost, and what it did not.** Four control jobs, about ¥0.9 of the ¥1.80. The science survived because
this lane's only reliable comparison is treatment against treatment (AUDIT 34.232): row 1 keeps its 69 and is
quoted against row 2's 100, both treatments, same 134 games, same commit. The control it lost was worth quoting
once, as a level, and this split's control has read 80, 81, 88, 89, 90, 91 across six dispatches — a band eleven
wins wide, which is why no conclusion here rests on it.

## 34.247 — The same 24 prompts, bought twice, moved one game: this lane's noise floor is measured

**The accident that makes the measurement.** The six-sentence bank's `put` entry is `bank-putmove-1.json`
**verbatim** — the register required it, so that the gated arm would reproduce the winning arm byte for byte on a
quarter of the split. It did: `prefix_chars` and the pack rendering are equal in **all 24 `put` games** between
`always-in@one` (run `44841962248`) and `always-in@kind` (run `44850240971`). The two arms carried different banks,
different labels and different dispatches, and for those 24 games they sent the model **the same bytes**.

**The reading.** 10/24 against 9/24. One game in twenty-four, 4.2 pp, on identical input, with the whole harness
held constant: same model, same split, same seed, same 50-step budget, same prompt.

**What it licenses.** Three things this lane has been arguing about for four rounds:

1. **A one- or two-game difference is nothing.** The difference between the one-sentence arm (112) and the
   two-sentence pair (109) is three wins and was already read as a tie; this says the tie is not close.
2. **Controls move by more than that** — 80/81/88/89/90/91 across six dispatches, i.e. up to eleven wins — so a
   control is a *band* and only a same-dispatch pairing is a comparison (AUDIT 34.232, 34.243).
3. **The six-arm/one-arm gap (24 discordant games, +8.96 pp, p = 0.014) is twice this floor** — measured on the
   same 134 games, so the comparison is like for like — and is the first length effect in the lane that clears its
   own noise rather than living inside it.

**What would be wrong to conclude.** That per-game outcomes are reproducible because the prompt is. They are not:
the same bytes won one game more in one dispatch than the other, and nothing in the artefact says which. The
measurement bounds the noise; it does not remove it, and the only defence is the paired design that repeats it.

## 34.248 — A pack is billed per call and a wrong pack is billed for fifty steps

**The reading.** R175's two arms carried 1,280 and 378 mean characters per game and cost $0.1879 and $0.2516. The
arm that rendered **902 characters less** cost **34% more**, and its per-win price is 2.7× the winning arm's:

| arm | mean pack | mean prompt | calls | bill | won | per win |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `always-in@one` | 489 | 4,563 | 3,004 | $0.1506 | 112 | **$0.00134** |
| six, ungated | 1,280 | 5,354 | 3,758 | $0.1879 | 100 | $0.0019 |
| six, gated by kind | 378 | 4,452 | 4,923 | $0.2516 | 69 | $0.0036 |
| `none` | 0 | 4,074 | 4,513 | $0.2245 | 91 | $0.0025 |

**The mechanism.** Cost is not a function of the prompt. Every call carries the pack, so length is a per-call
multiplier — but a lost game runs all fifty steps, so *being wrong* multiplies the number of calls. The gated arm
carried a pack 902 characters smaller and spent **2.9 M more prompt tokens** (12.66 M against 9.77 M over the same
134 games) because it made 1,165 more calls, each costing about 2,570 tokens of state the pack did not shrink.
**The most expensive memory in this lane is the one that is wrong in a way that costs steps**, and no length-based
cost model sees it.

**Why it belongs in the audit rather than the register.** It is the first measurement in this lane where an arm's
cost ranks *opposite* to its length, which is what a reader who budgets by tokens would get wrong — and the
dispatcher quotes a per-arm price before a sweep is bought (¥3.2 for two arms, i.e. ¥1.6 each). The six-sentence
arm came in at ¥1.34 and the gated one at ¥1.80, so the quoted price is a **floor for a winning arm and 12% short
for a losing one**. The arithmetic is not corrected here; it is bounded, and the bound is printed beside every
quote.

## 34.249 — A length-matched experiment needs a length counter, and the fixed prefix is not one

**The gap.** R176 asks whether a memory pays for what it *says* or for the evidence it *shows*, by carrying a
verbatim trajectory of **505 characters** where the one-sentence arm carried a statement of **489** — the same
information, the same corpus, the same model, 3.3% apart in length. Its registered void condition is a length
condition: *the arm's rendered prefix must exceed the control's by 505 characters and match the one-sentence arm's
within 20.* Nothing in the artefact could answer that. `prefix_chars` is the whole fixed prompt — system instruction,
few-shot examples, pack — so an arm whose pack was the wrong length still produces a plausible prefix, and the
comparison across dispatches has to subtract two means that each contain 3,965 characters of examples.

**What was added.** The episode record now carries `pack_chars`: the rendered length of the block that game was
shown, 0 for the control. It is the field the driver already computed (`len(pack)` in `run_episode`) and did not
keep, and `aggregate.py` prints it under `carried`:

```
  carried         always-in mean 1.0 entries over 134 games, {1: 134}
  pack chars      always-in 505 ch x134
```

**Why it is printed above the delta rather than in the appendix.** The order is the audit lesson from 34.243 applied
to a second question: the first thing a pack reading has to establish is that the pack was there, and the second is
that it was the pack it was registered with. `pack_entries` answers the first; `pack_chars` answers the second. A
gate that admitted one of the wrong six sentences has the same entry count as one that admitted the right one, and
an arm assembled from the wrong bank has the same label.

**The limits, stated.** Artefacts written before the field existed carry no `pack_chars`, and the report says
nothing about their length rather than reporting zero — the same rule `pack_entries` follows, and for the same
reason: a file that cannot answer is not a file that answered "no". R176's own artefacts predate the field, so its
length match is checked by hand from `prefix_chars` means this round and mechanically from the next one.

## 34.250 — A trace and a sentence are worth the same, and the aggregate tie is two opposite trades

**The reading.** R176 carried, in one dispatch, the verbatim trajectory the winning sentence was distilled from
(`banks/bank-rawput-1.json`, 505 rendered characters) and a control. Against that control the trajectory is worth
**+11.19 pp [+3.73, +18.66], p = 0.0038**; against the sentence it is worth **−2.99 pp [−3.73, +9.70], p = 0.445**.
The pair is length-matched to the byte: the arms' mean prefixes differ by 505.0 characters, which is the bank's
exact render.

**Why this is not the answer the literature predicts.** `arXiv:2605.12978` holds that abstraction is where a memory
loses its value. At matched length and matched content, abstraction costs nothing measurable here — so on this corpus
the claim is either false or about something this experiment did not vary. What is measurable is a *different*
difference, and it is per kind rather than in the mean:

| kind | sentence | trajectory | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `put` | 10/24 | 1/24 | +37.5 pp |
| `cool` | 20/21 | 19/21 | +4.8 pp |
| `heat` | 22/23 | 23/23 | −4.3 pp |
| `puttwo` | 16/17 | 17/17 | −5.9 pp |
| `clean` | 28/31 | 30/31 | −6.5 pp |
| `examine` | 16/18 | 18/18 | −11.1 pp |

**An arm that is worse than nothing on the games it came from.** The trajectory reads 1/24 on `put` against a control
of 5/24: a loss of four games on the one kind its evidence is about. This is the first arm in the lane to score below
its own control on a stratum while beating it on five others, and it is worth stating precisely what it means —
generalisation is not the issue, *transfer of the wrong part is*.

**The counters locate the mechanism without a transcript.** On `put` games the trajectory arm spent **49.5 of 50
steps** and **33.6 thoughts** per game, with **fewer invalid actions than either other arm** (6.8 against 8.8 for the
sentence and 8.1 for the control). Its failures were not syntactic: it had the format, took more deliberation and
pursued a plan about a toiletpaper and a toiletpaperhanger that were not in the room. The trace teaches the shape of
the solution and carries the nouns it was written about; the sentence names a repair and no object, so it can be
applied to whichever receptacle is present.

**What that changes in the product.** A store of traces is a legitimate memory at no measurable cost — and the best
demonstrated teacher of format in this lane (2.5 invalid actions per game against 3.4 for the sentence and 5.6 for the
control). A store of sentences is the better teacher of repair. They are complements, not rivals, and the mistake
this round retires is choosing between them on grounds of value: **choose on grounds of what the user's failures
are.** Format failures want a trace; blocked steps want a sentence.

**The instrument gap this reading exposed is fixed.** The registered void condition was a length condition that no
artefact field could answer (`prefix_chars` contains the few-shot examples as well). `pack_chars` is now recorded per
episode and printed under `carried` (AUDIT 34.249); R176's own length match is arithmetic on two prefix means.

## 34.251 — The second corpus section cost three guards, and the first one was a silent `min`

**The defect that had never fired.** `agent.py` computed its pass size as
`min(arguments.games, num_games)`. Every dispatch this lane has ever bought passed `--games 134` for a 134-game
section, so the `min` was the identity and nothing looked wrong. A dispatch that passed `--games 140` against the
same section would have driven **134** games, written `134/134` into the artefact, and printed a full-looking
rate for a budget the caller never received — the one place in the driver where a wrong number was silently made
smaller rather than refused. Both ceilings are now refusals (the table's, and the installed corpus's), and a
refused pass leaves no artefact behind.

**The table is now a measurement.** `SPLIT_SIZES` says `eval_out_of_distribution` 134, `eval_in_distribution` 140,
`train` 3,553 — counted with `find <section> -name game.tw-pddl | wc -l` rather than quoted. Two things read it:
`agent.py` refuses a `--games` beyond its section, and `aggregate.py` holds a join's tiling check to it. A table
that agrees with the corpus on the day it was typed and disagrees a release later is the worst kind of wrong
here, because every dispatch still runs and only the denominator moves. `scripts/check_split_sizes.py` is the
check: it counts the installed corpus and names every section that disagrees, with its own self-test on corpora
it builds (a short section, a matching one, a missing one) and 100% coverage under the same 95% floor as the
drivers. It runs twice — on the built corpora in `ci.yml` and against the fetched corpus in the `floor` job.

**The join rule was written too strictly and corrected by the experiment it was meant to serve.** The first
version of the guard refused any join that spanned two sections, on the grounds that a rate over two populations
is not a rate over either. That is true and it is not the whole truth: R177's entire purchase is a 274-game join
over two sections, because a second section is the only place this lane can buy resolution it does not already
own. A guard that refuses the design it was written for is a guard that gets deleted. The rule is now:
**a mixture is refused until it is declared, and once declared it is graded.** `--expect-splits` names the
sections; every episode carries the section its parent recorded; and `by_section` prints the paired delta of each
section beside the pooled one. That grading is not a diagnostic — it is R177's pre-registered question, since an
effect that exists in 134 held-out rooms and not in 140 seen ones is a property of a split rather than of memory.

**The leak guard turns on provenance, and provenance had to be written down.** A bank distilled from
`eval_in_distribution` and scored on it is the one leak this lane can commit while every number still looks
right. Nothing recorded which section a bank came from, so `distill.py` now writes `source.train_split` (read
from the artefacts' own `summary.split`, refused when a union mixes two), and the dispatcher refuses a
`--split` that equals a distilled bank's `train_split`. The guard is deliberately narrower than "any bank on any
section": a hand-written bank is a function of no section — one verbatim trajectory, one sentence — and refusing
it on `valid_seen` would refuse the arm R177 needs. The distinction is the presence of distill.py's own fields:
`episodes` says a bank was distilled from a set, and a distilled bank whose provenance is missing is refused
rather than trusted, because "cannot prove" is not "did not".

**The structural rule that would have caught 34.232 without paying for it.** The dispatcher's payload is a dict
and the workflow's inputs are text, so a key the YAML does not declare is dropped between them — which is exactly
how `--control-run` bought a treatment with no control while the command line said otherwise. `test_cli.py` now
builds the payload from two command lines that between them name every input, reads the declared keys out of
`alfworld.yml`, and asserts the difference is empty. Verified by deleting `split_games` from the YAML: two rules
fail, and the message names the key.

| what was added | the failure it makes impossible | held by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--games` beyond the section → refusal | a shortened pass reported as a full one | `test_agent.py::test_games_beyond_the_split_are_refused_rather_than_shortened` |
| `SPLIT_SIZES` + `check_split_sizes.py` | a table that drifts from the corpus | `test_check_split_sizes.py` (15 cases, 100% of the checker) |
| `--expect-splits` declaration + `by_section` | a pooled rate over two populations, quoted as one | `test_aggregate.py::test_an_undeclared_join_across_two_sections_is_refused` |
| `source.train_split` + the dispatch guard | a bank scored on the section that produced it | `test_distill.py::test_the_bank_records_the_section_it_read`, `test_alf_dispatch.py::SplitTest` |
| payload keys ⊆ workflow inputs | an input dropped between the dispatcher and the YAML | `test_cli.py::test_every_input_the_dispatcher_sends_is_one_the_workflow_declares` |

**Cost.** Nothing was bought: this round is instrument. The suite grew from 449 to 488 tests, coverage from 99.0%
to **98.9%** across a larger denominator, and every module is still at or above the 95% floor — with the new
checker at 100% because its failure branches are reached by handing it a case whose expectation is wrong rather
than excluded from measurement.

## 34.252 — The checker that assumed the download's layout failed on the first tree that ran it

**What happened.** The new guard was pushed, `ci.yml` passed — the unit step builds its own corpora, so the
checker was exercised there and nowhere else — and the `floor` job, which runs the checker against the *fetched*
corpus, reported all three sections missing:

> `FAIL eval_out_of_distribution: no valid_unseen/ under /home/runner/.cache/alfworld/data/json_2.1.1`
> `FAIL eval_in_distribution: no valid_seen/ under /home/runner/.cache/alfworld/data/json_2.1.1`
> `FAIL train: no train/ under /home/runner/.cache/alfworld/data/json_2.1.1`

The corpus was installed — 7,302 files extracted on that runner — and it was not where the checker looked.
`alfworld-download` puts the sections at `<data>/data/json_2.1.1` on the path this repository's development
corpus came from and somewhere else on the release the runner fetches, and the zip carries its own top-level
directory besides. The path had been copied from a working directory rather than measured.

**Why it is an audit entry and not a one-line fix.** It is the same class of defect as 34.246 and 34.251, in a
new place: a constant that was true where it was written, checked by a test that built its own world. The unit
test passed because the fixture wrote the layout the code expected — which is what a fixture always does. The
only thing that could have caught it is the job that runs against the real corpus, and that job exists because
the floor needs it; the checker was riding along.

**The fix, and the rule it leaves.** `locate()` searches for the section directories the table names instead of
assuming one level, and returns the shallowest match so that a fixture in a repository cannot outrank an
installed corpus. The download's layout is the download's business; finding the sections is the checker's. The
`--data` escape hatch stays for a corpus that is somewhere unusual, and it is what the development environment
uses.

| rule | where it now lives | what it prevents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| find the corpus, do not guess its root | `check_split_sizes.locate` | a guard that passes on one machine's folder tree |
| a missing home is "unknown", not "empty" | `locate` returns `None`, `main` exits 1 with a sentence | a zero that reads as a measurement |
| a fixture's layout is not evidence about the real one | the guard runs in the job that fetches the corpus | the green unit test that hid this for one push |

**What it cost.** One push, one red `floor` job, about four minutes of runner time, and no money — the job makes
no model calls. It is the cheapest possible version of this failure, and it was found before any dispatch read a
green tree as a licence to spend.

## 34.253 — The second section changed the denominator and not the conclusion, which is the result a replication is for

**The reading.** The one sentence, bought on `eval_in_distribution` in its own dispatch with its own control, and
joined to the held-out pair:

| reading | delta | 95% CI | p | mde |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| seen, 140 | **+25.71 pp** | [+17.86, +34.29] | < 0.001 | 13.28 pp |
| held-out, 134 | +17.91 pp | [+8.96, +26.87] | < 0.001 | 14.18 pp |
| pooled, 274 | **+21.90 pp** | [+15.69, +28.10] | < 0.001 | **9.70 pp** |
| seen − held-out | +7.80 pp | [−4.63, +20.27] | 0.226 | — |

**Why this is worth an entry rather than a line.** Three things were registered as possible and only one of them
happened:

1. *"≥ +12 pp on 274 games → the effect is larger than the held-out estimate and is a property of memory."* It
   read +21.90, and the seen section alone read +25.71 — larger than the held-out estimate, in the direction the
   registration called a finding rather than a failure.
2. *"< +5 pp, or a seen gain under +8 pp → the effect is a property of the held-out section."* Did not happen. This
   was the outcome the programme most needed to be able to see, and the design saw it clearly enough to exclude
   it: a seen-section gain of +25.71 is not a null.
3. *"the two sections differ"* — **not supported**: +7.80 pp, [−4.63, +20.27], p = 0.226. A 274-game design
   cannot separate 25.7 from 17.9, and the honest statement is that both carry the effect at a magnitude this
   design cannot distinguish.

**The composition finding, which was not registered and matters more than it looks.** `none` reads 53.57% on the
seen section and 65.67% held out. The entire difference is the mix of task kinds: `put` is 35/140 of the seen
games and 24/134 held out, and `put` is the one kind that no arm wins without the sentence (3/35, 2/24). Every
other kind agrees within a point across sections. So a pooled *rate* is an average over two mixtures while a
paired *delta* is not — which is exactly why `aggregate.py` grades by section instead of pooling silently, and it
is the second independent reason the guard from 34.251 was rewritten rather than kept as a refusal.

**The `examine` result, and why it is the strongest evidence the referent law has.** The control wins **all 31**
`examine` games in both sections; the sentence wins 27. That is −12.9 pp on the one kind with no placement step,
in two dispatches, on two sections, with the same sign. R175 read the same law from the other side (a
kind-description entry hurt the kinds it was written for); R176 read it from a third (a verbatim trace lost the
one kind whose nouns it carried). Three designs, one sentence of theory: **an entry pays where its referent is the
step that is failing, and costs its length everywhere else — and where it cannot be the failing step, it costs
more than its length.**

**What it cost, and what it did not.** ¥3.13 for the two arms against ¥2.8 quoted. The overrun is the control's:
$0.2574 for 140 games at 53.57% against $0.1801 for the same 140 at 79.29%, because a losing arm is billed for
all fifty steps of every game it loses (34.248). The instrument itself was unchanged this round — the section
plumbing from 34.251 was used exactly as written, including the graded join, and the `by section` lines are what
makes the composition finding visible at all.

## 34.254 — The bank said the clause named the run the entry came from, and it named the run the entry won in

**The defect.** R178's treatment arm appends 62 characters to the winning sentence. The sentence is entry 4 of
`banks/bank-44754440122.json`, distilled from run **44754440122**. The clause cites run **44841962248**, which is the
R174.1 held-out dispatch — the run in which *this entry* won 10 of its 24 `pick_and_place_simple` games. The bank's
`source.kind` read *"the winning sentence plus the run it came from"*. Both facts are true and they are not the same
fact.

**Why it is a defect and not a wording preference.** The whole round is about provenance, and the bank's own
provenance was the one place in the tree where a reader could be misled without any number moving. A citation of the
run the entry *came from* and a citation of a run it *won in* are different mechanisms — one points at the evidence,
the other at a validation — and WikiTrace's claim is about the first. Left as written, the document could have
quoted the reading as "an entry that carries its source" and been wrong about which source.

**What changed, and what did not.** `source.cited_run` and `source.distilled_from_run` are now both in the file, the
`kind` says *won*, the `note` names 44754440122 and says why the clause does not. Nothing in the prompt changed, so
nothing in the reading changed. Two tests hold the file: `test_the_citation_is_the_run_the_metadata_names` fails if
the clause and `cited_run` disagree or if the two run ids collapse into one, and
`test_the_treatment_names_a_run_and_the_control_names_no_number` fails if the length control gains a digit — a
"neutral" clause containing a number is a clause a reader can mistake for evidence.

**The general form.** A bank's `source` block was documentation when banks were pools of advice. It is now data about
claims the prompt makes, and the two fields that matter (`cited_run`, `false_by_construction`) are read by tests
rather than by `distill.validate_bank`, which must stay ignorant of them: a validator that refused an unfamiliar key
would make every new provenance field a code change, and the file-level claims of this lane have always been checked
in `test_banks.py`.

## 34.255 — A clause of 62 characters moves 55% of trajectories and 3.65 points of outcome, and the length it adds is free

**The reading.** Two arms of exactly 551 rendered characters, differing in one clause, on both sections:

| pairing | delta | 95% CI | p | discordant | mde |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a neutral clause − the sentence | −0.36 pp | [−4.74, +4.01] | 0.920 | 37 | 6.22 pp |
| the citation − the sentence | −4.01 pp | [−9.12, +0.73] | 0.127 | 47 | 7.01 pp |
| **the citation − the neutral clause** | **−3.65 pp** | **[−8.39, +1.09]** | 0.151 | 42 | **6.63 pp** |

**The length half is a null that retires a reading.** R174.2 established a per-entry tax (−3.4 to −3.7 pp per
sentence in a padded block) and this lane has since quoted its prices as if the tax were per character. It is not:
+62 characters inside one entry is 12.7% more prefix and **−0.36 pp**, with an interval that excludes any loss worse
than 4.7. The padding arms paid because they added **entries**. That distinction is what makes a citation affordable
at all — the clause is free and the citation is what costs — and it is why a length control for a clause experiment
must be a clause rather than a block.

**The citation half is negative, and it is not a delivery failure.** Engagement was **152/274 = 55.5%**: a
62-character suffix changed the action trajectory in more than half the corpus, hurting 26 games and helping 16. A
frozen model therefore does respond to a citation, and the response is net negative — which is the strongest form
this negative could take. A null attributable to the pack never arriving would have been uninterpretable; this one is
not.

**Where it sits, with its own floors.** On the games the neutral arm wins: **196/222 against 222/222** (−11.71 pp).
On the 52 it loses, the citation arm wins 16. `put` carries 19 of the 42 discordant pairs, net −5 games on 59, and
`put`'s own mde is **20.8 pp** — so the kind where the entry's referent lives is reported as a shape rather than a
finding. This is the third round in which a per-kind row would have been quotable and was not, and the reason is
arithmetic rather than caution.

## 34.256 — The floor is a property of the control, and this round halved it for one arm's price

**The measurement.** Two designs on the same 274 games:

| design | discordant games | mde |
| --- | --- | --- |
| treatment against the `none` arm of its own dispatch (R177) | 90 | 9.70 pp |
| treatment against another treatment (R178) | **42** | **6.63 pp** |

**Why this is the round's transferable result.** The lane had one lever for resolution: more games. R177 registered a
training-section subset at **¥10–50** for ≈ 6 pp. R178 reached 6.63 pp for **¥2.4**, because the quantity in the mde
is the *discordance* and a control contributes most of it. The `none` arm has read 80, 81, 88, 89, 90 and 91 wins on
the same 134 games across six dispatches — eleven wins of swing on identical inputs — while treatments repeat. A
delta against it is a band; a delta between two treatments is a comparison.

**The three consequences, in the order they bind.** (1) Every future row whose question is "which of two packs" should
be bought as one arm against an existing arm, not as two arms against two controls: it is half the price and a third
smaller floor. (2) The training-section row is retired, and with it the assumption that this lane's next problem is
sample size. (3) `aggregate.py --relabel` is now load-bearing rather than convenient: the pairing needs one rename per
slice keyed on the full path, because `arm-always-in-0.json` exists in every run directory the workspace holds, and a
pairing that silently drops four slices would report a 134-game answer with a 274-game label.

**The cost of the evidence.** $0.6664 (¥4.77) for 13,512 calls against ¥4.8 quoted, and the two arms' bills differ by
3.6% while their win rates differ by 3.65 pp — a losing arm is billed slightly more, which is the same asymmetry
34.248 recorded at a much larger size.

## 34.257 — A citation of a run that does not exist is worth a citation of a run that does, and that is WikiTrace's answer

**The arm.** One 62-character clause, `[source: one won pick_and_place_simple game, run 44800000000]`, appended to
the sentence R178 used, at the same 551 rendered characters. No artefact carries that run id, so the claim is false
and checkably false; the variant a product would ship — a real run that never carried the entry — is the same arm at
the model's level, because a frozen model reading a prefix cannot consult either.

| pairing | delta | 95% CI | p | discordant | mde |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fabricated − true | **+2.19 pp** | [−1.82, +6.20] | 0.363 | 34 | **5.96 pp** |
| fabricated − neutral | −1.46 pp | [−5.84, +2.92] | 0.566 | 36 | 6.14 pp |
| true − neutral | −3.65 pp | [−8.39, +1.09] | 0.151 | 42 | 6.63 pp |

**What the three rows say together, which none of them says alone.** A citation is worth less than a neutral clause
whether or not its referent exists (−1.46 and −3.65), and the two are indistinguishable from each other (+2.19,
inside a ±6 pp interval). So the quantity R178 measured is **form and not truth**: a bracketed claim about a run
costs a little, and the truth value of the claim does not survive the trip into a prompt. `put` — the kind the entry
names — is identical across the two citations, 16/59 and 16/59.

**Why this closes the mechanism rather than extending it.** WikiTrace's evidence link has two halves: the line, and
the descent to the run it names. This lane can buy the line and cannot buy the descent — there is nothing in a
frozen-model prompt to descend *with*. R178 priced the line at −3.65 pp; R179 shows the price does not depend on
whether the line is true. Anything that could recover WikiTrace's 79.5 → 90.2 therefore has to be inside the descent:
retrieval of the run, a verifier, or a policy trained to read citations — SkillRL's cold-start SFT, which the R177
pre-read in `COMPETITIVE.md` names as the structural difference between their harness and this one. That is a
statement about where the mechanism lives and it is now measured on both sides of the line.

**The instrument note.** The mde fell again, to **5.96 pp**, because this pair is *more* concordant than R178's (34
discordant games against 42): two arms that differ in a run id disagree less than two arms that differ in a clause's
kind. The floor is a property of the pair, not a constant of the design, which is the same lesson as 34.256 arriving
from a third direction — and it means the quoted floor for any future row has to be read off that row's own
discordance rather than off the last round's.


## 34.258 — Engagement is not a reading of the entry: a neutral clause moves as many trajectories as a citation does

The lane has used `engagement` — the share of games whose action digest changed — as the line between "the pack did
nothing" and "the pack was never delivered". R178 read 152/274 = 55.5% for a 62-character citation and concluded the
clause *is read*. R180 makes that conclusion untenable, and it does so with the lane's own artefacts rather than with
an argument.

| comparison | characters | clause that differs | engagement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R178: a true citation − a neutral clause | 551 vs 551 | the 62-character suffix | 152/274 = 55.5% |
| R178: the sentence − the neutral clause | 489 vs 551 | length *and* the suffix | 154/274 = 56.2% |
| R180: operation (1) only − the neutral clause | 551 vs 551 | the second operation | 146/274 = 53.3% |

**Three different single-clause edits, including one that replaces the citation with text saying the entry is not an
instruction, land within three games of each other.** If engagement measured whether the model read the clause, the
neutral note — which asserts that the entry is only a reference — would not be the *most* perturbing of the three.

**What engagement actually measures.** These games sit close to a decision boundary: a frozen model at temperature 0
given a 62-character suffix writes a slightly different first action, and the difference cascades through fifty turns.
The digest is sensitive to that cascade and blind to its cause. So engagement is a measure of **how many games are
near enough to a boundary for any perturbation to show**, which is a property of the corpus and the policy, not of the
clause.

**What this retires, and what it does not.** It retires the sentence "the citation is read, therefore a citation that
is wrong must cost" — the premise was never measured, only assumed from a number that a neutral note also produces. It
does not retire the *result*: the family's deltas are what they are, and the −3.65 pp for a true citation is still the
largest in the family and still inside its own mde. R179's "the model cannot tell a false citation from a true one"
was argued *from* the +2.19 pp gap and is unaffected; it was supported *by* the engagement reading and no longer
needs it.

**The replacement instrument, and its price.** A **same-bank re-dispatch** — the same file, the same 274 games, twice
— makes the true delta zero by construction, so whatever delta and whatever engagement it reports *is* the noise
floor. The lane has one such pair already, and it is too small to be the floor: the six-bank's `put` entry was the
winning sentence verbatim, so the gated arm reproduced the one-sentence arm's prompt **byte for byte in 24 games** and
those identical prompts scored 10 and 9 — **4.2 pp of sampling noise on 24 games**, which the whitepaper carries as
the lane's floor. Twenty-four games cannot put a number on a 274-game spread, and the pair reports no engagement at
all, so the quantity this section is about has never been measured. A full-size re-dispatch costs one arm (≈ ¥2.3 now
that the control side is shared). Until it is bought, every delta smaller than the family's 4.0 pp spread has to be
read as unresolved, which is what R178–R180 already do on their own intervals — the floor would make that a
measurement rather than a habit.

## 34.259 — 1,070 commands were dropped and the model was told `OK.`, and no field in the record could show it

**The defect.** `parse_reply` is the competitor's parser, transliterated, and it anchors at the first line: a reply
that opens with `> think:` is a thought, whatever the lines under it say. The competitor's own few-shot transcripts
write think-then-act in one turn — `react_put_0` has `> think: Now I find a spraybottle (2). Next, I need to take it.`
immediately followed by `> take spraybottle 2 from cabinet 2` — so the prompt teaches a format whose second line the
driver drops. The reference implementation then steps its environment with `N/A` and hands the model back the
environment's own `Nothing happens.`. This driver appended `OK.`, which is the examples' token for a thought that was
*only* a thought.

**The consequence.** The model read its own `> put …` followed by `OK.`, concluded the put had executed, and wrote
"The task is complete" until the turn budget ran out. In the 245 train games on disk: **1,070 commands dropped, in 72
of 72 `put` games** (14.9 per game), 30 of the other 173 games, and a mean trailing run of **9.7** victory claims in
a lost `put` game — 24 of those games are pure loops. `put` is the only kind destroyed because it is the only kind
where the model hedges before acting and the only kind that runs near the 50-turn cap (wins 31.7–35.9 turns, losses
50).

**Why four rounds could not see it.** Not because the transcripts were unavailable — they were, on every training run,
at no extra cost — but because **no field in the episode record could hold it**. `invalid_actions` counts what the
world refused; `stalls` counts three thoughts in a row; `steps` counts turns; a dropped command is none of the three.
The lane therefore read a *failure of delivery* as a property of the entry, and spent R177–R180 ablating 62 characters
inside a harness that was discarding fifteen commands per `put` game.

| the two ways a turn fails to reach the world | counted before | counted now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an invalid action: emitted, refused by the environment | `invalid_actions` | unchanged |
| a refused command: written under a thought, dropped by the parser | **nowhere** | `refused_actions`, `refused_samples` |

**The repair, and what it deliberately does not change.** The parser stays. Executing a command the first-line rule
refused would raise every arm's score and make this lane's numbers incomparable with the reference harness it is
built on — the entire value of the contrast is that the only thing differing between arms is what sits above the
transcript. What changes is the acknowledgement: `NO_OP = "Nothing happens."`, the corpus's own string, for a turn
whose command was refused; `OK.` stays for a thought that was only a thought. `aggregate.py` prints
`dropped <arm> n (x per call)` and prints `not counted` for a file that predates the field, because a `0` there would
mean "never counted" and not "never happened".

**What this does to every number already published.** Nothing is retracted and nothing is comparable across the line.
The +21.90 pp for the repair sentence was a *within-driver* contrast: both arms paid the same defect, and the
treatment plausibly reduced it, which makes the treatment's benefit real and its mechanism partly different from the
one registered. Its *level* (81%) and its *size* are both re-read by R181, which is the first round in this lane whose
control is bought on the repaired driver.

**The general lesson, which is the one that costs money.** A metric that cannot be recorded cannot be falsified. Three
rounds of this lane's most careful design — matched lengths, single clauses, registered bands, 274 games — were aimed
at a treatment effect while a delivery defect of 15 events per game sat in the same files, invisible because the
schema had no column for it. The first thing to check before ablating a treatment is whether the harness can represent
the way the treatment fails.

## 34.260 — Repairing the lie did not repair the behaviour, and the counter is what says so

R181 was registered as a repair with a mechanism: a command written under a thought was refused, the driver answered
`OK.`, the model believed it had acted, and `put` paid for it. The repair answered `Nothing happens.` instead. The
prediction was `put` up 6–22 pp.

**It read −1.69 pp** (20/59 against 21/59), and the same bank across the repair read **+1.82 pp [−2.55, +6.20]**,
p = 0.453, mde 6.22 — a null on the treatment's own pre-to-post comparison. The pre-registered refutation clause fired
exactly as written.

**What makes this a result rather than a failed round is the counter.** `refused_actions`, which did not exist before
this round, reads **11.64 per `put` game** in the treatment and **10.53** in the control — inside the 8–20 band the
registration named from the training transcripts — and **0.00 to 0.07** on the other five kinds. So the field measures
the defect it was built to measure, the defect is still there at the predicted rate, and the behaviour did not move.
Without the field, this round would have been indistinguishable from a repair that worked and a treatment that did not.

**The turn arithmetic names the real constraint.** A winning `put` costs 26.6 turns with 7.2 thoughts and 2.2
refusals; a losing one costs all 50, of which **32.0 are thoughts** and **16.5 are refused commands**. So a loss is
thirty turns of *thought, refused command, `Nothing happens.`* — and the shape repeats. The model does not adapt its
format to the answer it receives, which means the answer was never the binding constraint. The binding constraint is
that it writes a thought and a command in one reply on every turn, which the competitor's own few-shot examples teach
in `react_put_0`.

**Two general lessons, and the second one is about registration.**

*First*: a repair is not verified by the mechanism that motivated it, it is verified by the field that measures the
defect. The lane had no field for this defect for four rounds and spent ¥9.43 attributing a clause; it now has one,
and the field immediately falsified the causal story that motivated the repair. That is the instrument doing its job
in the same round it was built.

*Second*: a refutation clause written in advance is the only thing that made this round readable. "If `put` does not
move while `refused_actions` reads 8–20 per game, the false acknowledgement is not what kept `put` down" is a
sentence that cost one line at registration and now carries the whole interpretation. Without it, a null on `put`
would have been argued into a partial success through the pooled +1.82 pp.

**What the row does not license.** It does not license restoring `OK.` A driver that tells a model its dropped
command succeeded is a driver whose transcripts cannot be trusted, and the +28.10 pp it produced as a matched pair is
the number this lane will keep quoting — with the caveat that the control drew 81 of a band that runs 80 to 93.

## 34.261 — A prompt-level entry moves a format by fifteen per cent, and the residual is a floor not a lever

R182 registered three numbers and read one of them wrong in a way worth recording, because the wrong one is the only
one that speaks to mechanism. The arm put the format operation — *one command per turn, alone on its line* — into the
197-character slot R180 proved dead, at identical length and identical entry count, and predicted
`refused_actions` **below 5** per `put` game from a base of 11.64.

**It read 9.90.** The entry cut refusals by 15% and `put` gained seven games (17/59 → 24/59, +11.86 pp, inside a
per-kind mde of 19 pp); the pooled delta is **+3.65 pp [−1.09, +8.39]** at mde 6.78. So the intervention is real in
direction, unresolvable in size, and — the point — **it did not do what it said**. A model that had read the entry
would not write thought-and-command replies at all. It still writes 85% of them.

**Why this is the useful shape of a partial failure.** Three rounds now agree on the same structure:

| round | what changed | what the mechanism predicted | what the counter read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R181 | the answer a refused turn gets | the model stops believing it acted | refusals 11.64 (unchanged in kind) |
| R182 | an entry stating the format | refusals fall below 5 | refusals 9.90 (−15%) |
| both | — | — | `put` 20/59 then 24/59, neither resolved at 59 games |

A 197-character instruction inside a 551-character block moves a behaviour the few-shot examples teach by about one
turn in seven. That is a measurement of **how much leverage a prompt-level memory has over a format**, and the answer
is: not enough to close the gap, enough to be visible in a counter and invisible in a score.

**The floor, stated as a number the plan has to respect.** `put` is 59 of 274 games. At the discordance these pairs
produce, a `put`-only delta has an mde of **19 pp**; the pooled delta has an mde of **6.78 pp**. So the remaining
headroom — `put` at 40.7% against 88–100% on the other five kinds — can only be attacked by something that moves it
by more than a fifth of its range, or by an arm that increases the discordance on that kind rather than the game count.

**What that rules out, and it is most of the obvious queue.** More single-clause entries: eighteen games of spread
across seven arms, none resolved. More entries per pack: the per-entry price R174.2 measured (−3.4 to −3.7 pp) exceeds
anything a second entry has been shown to buy. Bigger `n`: 274 games already costs ¥2.2 a round and the split has 274
in it.

**What it leaves.** One intervention is large enough to matter and has never been run: executing the command that the
first-line rule refuses. That is not a memory arm — it changes the harness for every arm — so it has to be registered
as a **channel**, with both arms re-run on it and the divergence from the reference stated in the same sentence as the
result. Its expected size is the whole of the format's cost: a lost `put` game spends 16.5 of its 50 turns on commands
that never ran, so a channel in which they run has roughly a third of the budget back on the one kind that needs it.

## 34.262 — The channel: what changes when the reader changes, and what has to be refused so it cannot be missed

34.261 left one intervention standing — execute the command the first-line rule refuses — and one requirement with
it: because it changes the harness under **both** arms, it cannot be registered as an arm. This entry records the
design that makes that distinction mechanical rather than editorial.

**The code path, and how small it is.** `parse_reply` is untouched. `refused_command` is untouched — it already
returned the command, which is what made R181 and R182 readable. The only change is in `run_episode`, at the point
where a thought reply was answered with `Nothing happens.`:

```python
refused_here = refused_command(reply)
if refused_here is not None and parser == ANY_LINE_PARSER:
    recovered += 1
    if len(recovered_samples) < REFUSED_SAMPLES:
        recovered_samples.append(refused_here)
    action = refused_here
    break
```

The command leaves by the same door an action leaves by — `env.step` — so the turn is counted as an action turn, the
model is answered with an observation rather than a no-op, and `steps`, `actions`, `invalid_actions` and `digest` all
keep their meanings. Nothing is re-read and nothing is invented: the parser found this command and refused it, and this
channel is the one where the refusal is not the end of the turn.

**Two counters, because one event has two sides.** `refused_actions` counts a command the rule *dropped*;
`recovered_actions` counts one it *would have* dropped and the channel executed. One reply is one event, counted on
whichever side of the parser it fell. That is the instrument the round is read with: if the second channel recovers
roughly what the first dropped (11.64 and 10.53 per `put` game), the two channels drove the same model behaviour and
the difference between them is the harness. If it does not, they drove different behaviour and the cross-channel rows
are descriptive rather than causal — a distinction the round registers before it buys.

**Four refusals, each closing a way of pooling two harnesses without noticing.**

1. **A channel in every episode**, not only in the summary. A join that pooled two readers is otherwise undetectable
   below the file level, and the artefact is what a later round reads.
2. **A channel in every label** (`always-in@anyline`, `none@anyline`). Two channels of one arm are two harnesses; a
   label that did not move would leave `aggregate.py` grouping them, and its doubled-games refusal arrives after both
   were paid for. The channel moves the control's label too, unlike a pack knob: it does not select from the pack, it
   changes what the environment does with a reply.
3. **`aggregate.py` refuses a span it was not told about** (`--expect-parsers`), the same rule `--expect-splits`
   applies to a pooled rate over two corpus sections: legal, sometimes the point, never silent.
4. **`aggregate.py` refuses one label spanning two channels at all**, with no override. A section mixture is a
   population claim; a channel mixture under one label is an arm that is two harnesses, which is not a claim.

**What the round can and cannot be compared to.** The reference channel stays the default forever, and every artefact
written before this entry is read as the reference channel rather than as unknown — the only reader that existed is
written down in the code, so reading the absence as a guess would be inventing ambiguity. What the round cannot do is
put a second-channel number beside a published row: no published ALFWorld row was measured on a reader this lane built,
and the comparison the round is actually for is *its own arms, both channels* — which is why it buys the control again
rather than reusing R181's.

**The prediction this is built to test.** The memory effect on the reference channel is **+29.20 pp**. Part of that
could be a workaround: an entry that tells the model how to write around a reader that drops its command. If it is, the
entry's value falls on the second channel and the registered band is **+10 to +25 pp**. If the effect holds at +29, the
workaround reading is refuted and what the bank carries is procedure rather than syntax. Either way the round answers a
question eleven renderings could not, because the eleven were all inside the harness.

## 34.263 — One field of a driver is worth more than eleven prompt rounds, and the residual is exploration

R183 executed the command the first-line rule refuses. The result is the largest effect this lane has measured since it
started measuring anything: **+9.85 pp** on the bank arm (230 → 257 of 274) and **+17.15 pp** on the control (150 → 197),
both at p < 0.001, against a family of eleven prompt renderings that never resolved a pair inside ±3.65 pp.

**The three readings, and what each one is a claim about.**

| reading | delta | what it is about |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bank arm, two readers | **+9.85 pp** [+5.47, +14.23] | the cost of the format to a model that carries an entry |
| control, two readers | **+17.15 pp** [+10.22, +24.09] | the cost of the format to a model that carries nothing |
| the memory effect on the second reader | **+21.90 pp** [+16.06, +27.74] | what the entry is worth when the format costs a third less |

The third row is the one the round was registered for. The effect on the reference channel is **+29.20 pp**; on a reader
where the dropped command executes it is **+21.90 pp**. So a quarter of the entry's apparent value was a workaround — an
instruction that taught the model to write around a parser that was throwing its command away — and three quarters was
not. The registered band was **+10 to +25 pp** and it held; a reading at the top of it would have refuted the workaround
reading, and this one does not.

**The registry's own refutation clause fired, and the denominator is the reason.** `recovered_actions` reads **4.17** per
`put` game on the bank arm where 8 to 15 was registered. The clause said that would mean the two channels met different
model behaviour. Per **model turn** the arms recover 0.0554 and 0.0740 — 25% apart — and the per-game rate is 2.5× apart
because a won `put` is **13.1 turns** on the bank arm against **21.8** on the control. The per-game rate was measuring the
format and the number of chances to write it in one number, which is the same error as quoting tokens per document when
the documents differ in length. Recorded as a post-hoc correction, not as a prediction that held: the clause fires, the
cross-channel rows are descriptive, and +21.90 pp is the surviving registered quantity.

**`put` was never the task.** 24/59 → **50/59** on the bank arm, 4/59 → **35/59** on the control. The control's `put` has
been on the board since R180 as the row no published memory paper reports: a frozen model at **6.8%** on one of six task
kinds. On this reader it is **59.3%**. A deficit that four rounds of prompt text could not move was, to two thirds of its
size, the reader rather than the task or the memory.

**And the floor that is left is a different floor.** Nine `put` games still lose all 50 turns: **17.7 thoughts** and
**15.0 recovered commands** per game, against a won `put` of 13.1 turns and 1.4 thoughts. The commands now execute, so
they are not lost to the format any more; the games still do not finish because the model spends a third of its budget
narrating and does not adapt. That is **exploration depth**, and it is the first question in this lane's queue that a
prompt-level entry is the wrong instrument for: R180 and R182 spent ¥4.5 proving an entry can move a format by 15%, and
the remaining 9 games are a model that keeps talking after it has been told what happened.

**What cannot be claimed.** The 93.80% and 96.27% are this lane's numbers on a reader this lane built. No published
ALFWorld row was measured on it, so they cannot be placed on the prompt-only board — and placing them there would be the
category error `COMPETITIVE.md` AM.22 spends a section on. What the round licenses is the *internal* comparison it was
registered for: same bank, same games, two readers, and a memory effect that falls from +29.20 to +21.90 when the harness
stops leaking.

## 34.264 — A counterfactual over a sampled policy is a prediction, and the lane called it a floor

R184's registration computed each arm's score at a cap of thirty from that arm's own cap-50 episode records, as
`|{e : e.won and e.steps <= 30}|`, and then wrote the number down twice as **"a floor no behaviour can fall below and a
ceiling only behaviour can raise"**. The arithmetic is exact: it is a deterministic function of records already paid
for. The word is not.

A language-model policy is **sampled**. A game that won at step 22 on the fifty-step pass may be lost outright on the
thirty-step pass — same arm, same bank, same channel, different draw — so the counterfactual is a *prediction about a
sampled trajectory*, with the policy's own variance around it, and not a set-inclusion argument. The round returned
**240** and **156** against predictions of **242** and **157**: two and one games *below*, on 274 games each.

**What the mislabelling cost.** Nothing in the decision — the registered bands (246–262, 162–190) were wide enough to
fail on a 2-game shortfall, and they failed, which is the right verdict either way. What it cost is the sentence a
reader would have quoted if the arms had landed *above*: "the excess is behaviour, because the number is a floor" is a
claim the design cannot support. The excess would have been behaviour *plus* sampling noise, and separating them needs
either a seed-matched re-run or a paired comparison — which is what the same round also reports and which no bound
argument was needed for.

**The general form, because this lane has now made the same class of error three times.** R183 registered a per-*game*
rate for a quantity that was per-*turn* and caught it in the readback (34.263). R184 registered a counterfactual as a
*bound* for a quantity that is a *prediction*. R180 registered "operation (2) is worth something" for an artefact that
measured its absence. Each time the artefact was right and the sentence about the artefact was wrong, and each time the
repair is the same: **name the quantity's type before naming its value** — rate, bound, prediction, or estimate — because
the four support different verdicts from the same number.

**What is now enforced instead.** The join refuses a cap span until it is declared, because a cap is a harness and its
price is asymmetric between arms (15 games against 40 at cap 30). The readback quotes each arm against **itself** at the
other cap, and the cross-arm delta at the new cap is printed with the frozen value beside it: **+30.66 pp observed
against +31.02 pp predicted**, so the widening is the cap's arithmetic to within 0.36 pp and no part of it is memory.

## 34.265 — The refusal that would have been silent had no test, and the seven places it now lives

R184 makes `--max-steps` a variable for the first time in this lane's history. Every earlier reading ran at the
environment's own fifty. A variable cap turns four previously harmless facts into failure modes, and each of them is
silent unless something refuses it:

| where | what it would do | what now refuses it | how it is tested |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/alf_dispatch.py` | `--max-steps 30.0` reaches `agent.py` as `type=int` after the environment install, in eight jobs, with the money committed | a whole-number check before the API call | `test_a_step_cap_that_is_not_a_whole_number_is_refused` |
| `scripts/alf_dispatch.py` | `--max-steps 2` succeeds and returns eight zeroes that read as a mechanism that does not work | a check against the shortest win the corpus has recorded — three steps in 6,096 episodes | `test_a_step_cap_below_the_shortest_recorded_win_is_refused` |
| `eval/drivers/alfworld/aggregate.py` | one label driven at two caps averages into a rate nobody designed | `label_caps`, refused outright | `test_one_arm_cannot_span_two_caps` |
| `eval/drivers/alfworld/aggregate.py` | a join across caps prints a delta that is partly arithmetic | `--expect-caps`, required to state the span | `test_a_join_that_spans_two_caps_is_refused_until_it_names_them` |
| `eval/drivers/alfworld/aggregate.py` | a declared span the artefacts do not have | the declaration is checked against the files | `test_a_declared_span_the_slices_do_not_have_is_refused` |
| `eval/drivers/alfworld/aggregate.py` | `summary.max_steps` arriving as a string and compared to an integer three checks later | a type check at read time | `test_a_cap_that_is_not_a_number_is_refused` |
| `eval/drivers/alfworld/aggregate.py` | `--expect-caps 3o` raising from `int()` three frames down, which reads as a crash | a refusal in the declaration parser | `test_a_declared_cap_that_is_not_a_number_is_refused` |

**The fourth row is the one that mattered before the round started.** R184's primary design compares each arm against
*itself* at two caps, and the join will now refuse exactly that comparison unless the span is declared — which is the
discipline the registration wanted and could not state as an intention. A guard that only exists in a document is a
guard that the next round forgets; the seven rows above are the ones that survive an editor.

**The sixth row is a lesson about JSON.** `parser` arrives from the same place and had the same hole, and nobody noticed
because a channel name is always a string and the comparison it feeds is a set membership. `max_steps` feeds an integer
comparison, so a malformed artefact would have been *read as a different cap* rather than as malformed — a defect with
no symptom until somebody compares two readings and cannot reproduce the delta.

## 34.266 — A guard that would have refused the round it was built for

R185 added `bank_digest` because two banks of 551 characters under one label were indistinguishable in every field the
join read. The first implementation put the field in the **episodes** and refused any label whose episodes carried more
than one value. That is correct for R185, which swapped one bank for another.

It is wrong for R186, which the same afternoon registered: a bank with two 354-character entries tagged to disjoint sets
of kinds, selected by `--gate-kind`, so that every game still reads 551 characters but `put` reads a different one. Under
the guard as written, that round's own artefact would carry two `bank_digest` values inside one label and the join would
refuse to load it — **the guard would have refused the round it exists for**, and the failure would have appeared as a
dispatch that ran, billed and could not be read.

**The repair is a distinction the first version collapsed.** A pass is handed **one bank** and a game reads **one pack**.
`bank_digest` is now a summary field (one per run, which is what a label groups on) and `pack_digest` a per-episode field
(which under a gate changes with the kind, and is the only record that says so). Five tests cover it, one of them the
gated shape: several `pack_digest` values, one `bank_digest`, no refusal.

**The general form.** A guard is a claim about what may vary inside a unit, and the unit has to be the one the experiment
varies. R183's channel guard was right because a channel cannot vary inside a pass. R184's cap guard was right for the
same reason. The bank guard was wrong because the bank is the thing that *can* vary inside a pass, and a gate is the
mechanism for making it vary. **The test that would have caught it is the next round's shape, written before the next
round's design is final** — which is what this audit entry is, one round late.

## 34.267 — Three registration errors in three rounds, and the template defect behind them

R184 registered a counterfactual as a **bound** for a quantity that is a **prediction** over a sampled policy. R185
registered a **per-lost-game** mean for a treatment whose purpose is to shrink the number of lost games — nine became
three, and the mean rose while the count of bad games fell from eight to three. And R185 also registered a follow-up
cell — *both tails at 551 characters* — that **cannot be built**: 157 + 197 + 197 is 551 characters of entry in a
354-character slot.

Three rounds, three errors, and none of them in the code. The class is: **a registration is prose, and nothing executes
it.** The readings are checked against artefacts; the *design* is not checked against arithmetic or against the shape of
the quantity it names. Two rules follow, and both are now part of how a registration is written rather than how it is
reviewed:

1. **Every registered cell must be computable, before it is bought, from an artefact that exists** — a script, a stored
   run, or the bank file itself. R185's impossible cell would have failed at the first `len()`.
2. **A rate's denominator must be fixed by the design.** If the treatment changes how many units exist — lost games,
   refused replies, replays — the reading is a **count** (eight bad games became three) or a rate over a denominator the
   treatment cannot move (turns, not lost games), and never a mean over the survivors.

The first rule already exists in this lane in two places and was not generalised: the price of a round is quoted before
the dispatch, and the pack's rendered length is asserted in `test_banks.py` before the arm is bought. Both are
*computable-before-buying* checks. The registration template now carries the third.

## 34.268 — A pool that is nine-tenths one stratum, read three times as if it were a population

`recovered` — the count of replies shaped *thought, then command* — was introduced in R183 as the second reader's
counterpart to `dropped`, and read in R185 as evidence that the pack's format clause was doing work: 269 → 137, "the
change is not local to `put`". R186's registration then wrote its third refutation clause on the same counter: a band of
250 to 320, with the inference that a value below it would mean the clause was never the cause.

The band was met by nothing and could not have been. The decomposition R186 bought:

| | `put` | other five | pool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R183 (clause on every pack) | 246 | 23 | 269 |
| R185 (clause replaced everywhere) | 132 | 5 | 137 |
| R186 (clause on five packs, precondition on `put`) | 133 | 35 | 168 |

**The pool is 91% `put` in R183 and 79% in R186**, so it is not a population at all. 168 = 133 + 35, and the 101-game
fall against R183 is 113 games *inside* `put` offset by 12 outside it. In a round whose design deliberately removes the
clause from `put` and from nowhere else, a pool band below 250 is not a refutation — it is the design, restated.

Three defects, in the order they did damage:

1. **The reading.** "The change is not local to `put`" was 86% wrong: 114 of the 132-game fall was `put`.
2. **The registration.** A band over a pool is a band over one kind whenever one kind holds the events. The cell is
   computable before buying — run the decomposition on the previous round's artefact — and under rule 1 of 34.267 it
   should have been.
3. **The instrument.** `aggregate.py` printed the pool number and only the pool number, so two consecutive rounds read
   it as a statement about the pack. It now prints each kind's own count beside that kind's own calls, and prints nothing
   when a file predates the field. Seven tests (`RecoveredScopeTest`), one of them the "eight-times-different denominator"
   case that a shared call count would have hidden.

**What the counter actually measures, now that it has been read correctly.** On the `any-line` channel the shape the
clause forbids is executed anyway, so the clause's 197 characters buy **no wins** (R185 `put` 56 with the precondition,
R186 `put` 56 with it, R183 `put` 50 — the difference is the precondition, not the clause). On the reference channel the
same shape is **dropped**, which is the +9.85 pp of R183. And a control with no pack produces **615** of the events,
because it flails for 23.8 turns a game. `recovered` meters the **reader**, and the memory only through it.

This is the third member of the class named in 34.267 — a mean over lost games, a counterfactual over a sampled policy, a
band over a pool — and the class has one sentence: **a denominator fixed by the outcome is a number about the treatment
you applied, not the thing you measured.**

**The round's own power is reported as what it is.** The scoped bank reads +2.55 pp over R183's single-entry bank with a
95% interval of [+0.00, +5.47], bootstrap p = 0.081 and **mde 3.96 pp**: 274 games cannot separate them. The claim this
audit will defend is the compositional one — the five byte-identical kinds moved **one game**, and the `put` gain
replicated at identical transitions on an independent sample (16 against 4 pooled, p = 0.0118) — and not "the scoped bank
is better than the bank it came from", which needs the 274 games R190 already plans to buy.

## 34.269 — A provenance hash that hashed the wrong thing, and a registration cell nobody multiplied

R187 moved one variable: the tags. `bank-putscope-2` gives the precondition to `put`; `bank-putscope-3` gives it to
`put`, `cool`, `heat` and `puttwo`. Both banks hold **the same two 354-character sentences**, so `digest_of(rules)` —
which hashed the texts — returned **the same `bank_digest`** for both, `eed9bea6…`, in all eight summaries of both rounds.

Three consequences, in the order they matter:

1. **The field could not see the only variable the round moved.** A reader comparing the two rounds' headers would
   conclude the second re-ran the first.
2. **The guard built on that field could not fire.** R185's join refuses a label spanning two banks; two banks with the
   same text are one digest, so a real bank swap passes it silently.
3. **The pack digests *were* different** — `90c0688f` for `clean`/`examine`, `5fb4c464` for the other four — which is
   what made the defect detectable at all: the pack field is per game and the bank field is per run, and only one of them
   was telling the truth.

The repair is `bank_digest_of(rules, kinds)`: each entry's **sorted tag set** with its text, so the two banks now read
`349213e8…` and `4efb1eba…`, and a re-ordered `kinds` list is still one bank because a tag list is a set. Three tests.
Every `bank_digest` recorded before this round identifies a **text** and not a bank, and the tables that quote one say so.

**The second defect is the one 34.267 predicted and did not prevent.** Reading 5 of R187 registered "two `pack_digest`
values in the 164:110 proportion the tags imply". The four targeted kinds are 59 + 46 + 39 + 41 = **185** games and the two
frozen ones are 58 + 31 = **89**. The cell was arithmetic, it was wrong by 21 games, and the artefact recorded the right
numbers. Rule 1 of 34.267 — *every registered cell must be computable before it is bought from an artefact that exists* —
would have caught it: **`aggregate.py` prints the per-kind game counts on every reading, and R186's own reading prints
them**. The rule is therefore amended to name the check rather than the principle: *a registered cell that is a count of
kind membership is copied from the previous round's per-kind table, not estimated.*

**What the round incidentally measured, and the reason it belongs in an audit.** R187's `put`, `clean` and `examine`
carried byte-identical packs to R186's and moved **−3, −2, +1** — **−4 games over 117** — while R186's five frozen packs
had moved **+1 over 215** against R183. Two draws of the same quantity, five games apart. So the same-prompt band of this
harness is **±5 games over 274**, not the ±1 that R186's own draw suggested, and every claim in this record below that
width on a single pass is a claim about one afternoon. The R186 headline survives (it is +67 against a control and +7
with a replicated per-kind mechanism); the "not worse by two games" phrasing does not.

## 34.270 — Ten losses, two families, and a report that called all of them "lost"

Every reading this lane has printed since R171 has reduced an episode to a boolean. That is right for a win count and
wrong for a diagnosis, and R186 is where the bill arrived: ten losses, reported as ten, of which **five never acted**.

The two families, read off the recorded per-episode fields:

| family | games | environment steps | thoughts | invalid actions | last line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| never acted | 5 | 4, 6, 16, 23, 26 | 46, 44, 34, 27, 24 | 4, 1, 1, 17, 20 | `Nothing happens.` in four |
| acted every turn | 5 | 49, 49, 49, 50, 50 | 1, 0, 1, 0, 1 | 2, 14, 2, 6, 0 | a room description in three |

The separation is not a mean with a wide spread; the two groups do not overlap on either coordinate. And the winning
side fixes the boundary: **no won game in 264 carries twenty thoughts**, and none carries ten invalid actions. So a
single threshold (`THOUGHT_HEAVY = 20`) separates the class, and `aggregate.py` now prints it beside the win count.

**Why this is an instrument defect and not a report-writing preference.** The lane has spent three rounds on the *harm*
of a memory — R185's −18 games, R187's −10 — and every one of those conclusions was computed over "lost" games. If half
the losses in an arm are games where the model never touched the world, then any statistic conditioned on losses is a
statistic over two populations, and the harm attributed to a pack can be the pack failing to suppress a rumination loop
that the control also has. The counter is the cheapest way to keep that from happening again: it is computed from two
integers already in every episode record, and it costs one line.
